title: Facebook Product Catalog | Nosto Help Center
text: Facebook Product Catalog | Nosto Help Center Skip to main content English Français Deutsch English English Français Deutsch English Search for articles... All Collections Facebook Manuals Facebook Product Catalog Facebook Product Catalog Learn more about Facebook Product Catalog and how Nosto handles product catalog management for your ads Written by Alina Marques June 17, 2020 A Facebook product catalog is a container that holds information about the products you want to advertise or sell across Facebook and Instagram. In e-commerce, this is commonly a replica of a site's product inventory. All customers who use Nosto's Facebook integration, can make use of Product Catalogue, which is required for product based Facebook & Instagram ads and features such as Instagram Shopping or Facebook shop. Product catalog is uploaded to Facebook automatically if the integration mode for product catalog management is selected. The catalogue named Nosto Default Product Catalogue is uploaded and continuously updated every three hours, whereas full uploads updating all details are done weekly. This means that when products are sold out on your site, prices dropped or other details adjusted, changes in products are reflected almost immediately in your ads or other Facebook features you might use, such as Shopping on Instagram. The catalogue is updated as long as your Nosto account is connected to Facebook. If the default catalogue is not available under your business manager, review in the dashboard the time when catalog was updated the last time and if this indicates an error, reach out to our support. Removing Rejected Products Products that violate Facebook’s ad policy are rejected from ads and repeated violations might lead to banning an ad account. Nosto’s integration helps you to mitigate the risk by exposing violating products in the rejected products view in the dashboard and by exposing simple to use inclusion and exclusion rules to narrow down your product inventory. Google Product Categories for Facebook By default Nosto uses your product's Google Category when generating pixel events and product catalogues in Facebook. If your product doesn't have a Google Category or this is not included in the implementation, we fall back in the product's category, which according to Nosto's tagging structure, follows the website's navigational hierarchy. The format commonly looks like something below, assuming product range Canoes are under sub-category Boats and under Outdoor main category on the website. /Outdoor/Boats/Canoes Google Category is a pre-defined and fixed taxonomy structure by Google which originally helps to ensure that your Google search ads are shown with the right search results. The same detail and taxonomy structure can be used to power dynamic ads also on Facebook. To demonstrate the difference, the same taxonomy following the Google Category structure for Canoes would be as below, 1124 or Sporting Goods > Outdoor Recreation > Boating & Water Sports > Boating & Rafting > Canoes How to Map the Google Category To set the Google Category, review and update if needed your Nosto integration and product tagging to set the google_category attribute to the appropriate value in the Google product taxonomy . You may either use a number (e.g. 1604) or description (e.g. Apparel & Accessories > Clothing). For more information about Nosto integration and product tagging, please refer to our tagging guide or reach out to our support. How to Review the Google Category in Nosto Tagging Use debug toolbar or review page source to review the tagging and format. Common Errors and Debugging When Google Category is not present and Nosto falls back to regular category, Facebook still tries to interpret the product category following the Google standard. By default this is harmless and caused by a mismatch between expected value, which might trigger notification emails or similar updates when logging in to the business manager. You can adjust the notification settings in business manager to tune down unnecessary notifications, which can be triggered multiple times a day as Nosto updates your product catalogue automatically when changes occur in your shop platform (e.g. product availability, price) Mapping Google Category accordingly for Facebook ads might improve ad delivery as it could help Facebook to interpret taxonomies following Google's standard, but on the contrary it doesn't have a negative impact nor it prevents running dynamic product ads. Product Catalog Permission Error The Facebook user that connects Nosto to your ad account needs to be an admin of the catalogue in order for us to automatically update it. When the integration is enabled, access-level is reviewed, but access can be also revoked for example if a Facebook user is removed. If there is an error message indicating a potential update error view the product catalogue in your Business Settings on Facebook's Business Manager. Click on the Add People button to give the user the Product Catalogue Admin role. Then confirm that the user has the Catalogue Admin role. We periodically check the product catalogue's permissions, so it may take a few hours before the Product Catalogue Permissions Error message disappears. Did this answer your question? You can use the Notifications sub-API to receive push notifications when data changes in your Merchant Center accounts. Instead of periodically polling the API to detect changes, you can subscribe to real-time event feeds delivered directly to an HTTPS endpoint that you configure. The Notifications sub-API supports notifications for: Product status changes : Receive real-time alerts when a product approval status changes (for example, when a product becomes disapproved or approved) across any of your linked accounts or sub-accounts. Account service changes : Receive real-time alerts when an AccountService resource is created, updated, or deleted (such as when an account service relationship is established, modified, or removed). Prerequisites & callback URI setup To receive push notifications, you must provide a callBackUri . Your callback URI must meet the following requirements: Must be a publicly accessible HTTPS address with a valid SSL certificate signed by a recognized certificate authority. Must accept HTTP POST requests with the Content-Type header set to application/json . Must return one of the following HTTP status codes to acknowledge that the notification was received: 102 200 201 202 204 You can use the same callback URI for multiple subscriptions. To minimize the load on a single endpoint, use a unique callback URI per advanced account and event type. Manage subscriptions The Notifications sub-API provides methods to create, list, retrieve, update, and delete notification configurations. Create a subscription Subscription creation is specific to the event type you want to receive. Each event type requires different configuration fields and delivers distinct payload structures. To learn how to create subscriptions and view sample requests for each event type, see the respective guides: Subscribe to product status changes Subscribe to account service changes List subscriptions To list all notification subscriptions for an account, send a GET request to the notificationsubscriptions collection: GET https://merchantapi.googleapis.com/notifications/v1/accounts/ {ACCOUNT_ID} /notificationsubscriptions Retrieve a subscription To get details for a specific subscription, use the subscription's resource name: GET https://merchantapi.googleapis.com/notifications/v1/accounts/ {ACCOUNT_ID} /notificationsubscriptions/ {SUBSCRIPTION_ID} Update a subscription To update the callback URI for an existing subscription, send a PATCH request with an update_mask specifying the fields to update: PATCH https://merchantapi.googleapis.com/notifications/v1/accounts/ {ACCOUNT_ID} /notificationsubscriptions/ {SUBSCRIPTION_ID} ?update_mask=callBackUri { "callBackUri" : " https://example.com/updated-callback " } Delete a subscription To stop receiving notifications, delete the subscription: DELETE https://merchantapi.googleapis.com/notifications/v1/accounts/ {ACCOUNT_ID} /notificationsubscriptions/ {SUBSCRIPTION_ID} Decode notifications When an event occurs, Google delivers a notification to your registered callBackUri . The push notification arrives in a JSON envelope with a base64-encoded data payload: { "message" :{ "data" : "{base64_encoded_string}" }} Decode the data string to access the JSON event payload. The following sample Spring Boot controller shows how to receive and decode push notifications: @RestController public class ExampleController { @RequestMapping ( value = "/push" , method = RequestMethod . POST , consumes = { "application/json" }, produces = { "text/plain" }) @ResponseStatus ( HttpStatus . OK ) public void handleNotification ( @RequestBody String message ) { JSONObject jsonObject = new JSONObject ( message ); JSONObject jsonMessage = jsonObject . getJSONObject ( "message" ); String encodedData = jsonMessage . getString ( "data" ); byte [] decodedBytes = Base64 . getDecoder (). decode ( encodedData ); String decodedPayload = new String ( decodedBytes ); // Process decodedPayload according to the registered event type } } Next steps To configure subscriptions and handle decoded payloads for specific events, see: Get push notifications for product status changes : Learn how to subscribe to product disapproval and approval updates and parse the ProductStatusChangeMessage payload. Get push notifications for account service changes : Learn how to subscribe to account relationship updates and parse the ResourceChangeMessage payload. Page Summary outlined_flag This guide explains how third-party providers can use OAuth 2.0 to request access to their clients' merchant accounts through their apps. Apps accessing the Merchant API need to be verified to avoid limitations, a process that usually takes 3-5 business days. Incremental authorization is recommended during setup to prevent scope selection issues and ensure the app receives necessary permissions. All Merchant API requests must be authorized using OAuth 2.0 with a valid access token, obtainable through the described authorization flow. Developers can find resources such as OAuth 2.0 scope information and authorization samples within the guide for implementation. This guide explains how to use OAuth 2.0 to request access to other parties' merchant center accounts. If you're a third-party provider, use this workflow to let your app request access to your clients' Merchant Center accounts. If you're developing an in-house app that needs access to only your Merchant Center account, see access your account instead. Request app verification Apps that access the Merchant API must go through the OAuth verification review process. Unverified apps will receive warnings and have limited functionality . An app is anything with a unique OAuth 2.0 Client ID in Google Cloud. The verification process typically takes 3-5 business days. To learn more and to submit a request for verification, see verification for apps . This policy applies to all apps. We recommend all apps undergo the verification process as early as possible to avoid business interruptions. Get OAuth scopes Set up incremental authorization to avoid issues with scope selection. All OAuth scopes are unselected by default in the consent screen for your app if you request more than one. When your app presents the consent screen to a user, the user has to manually select each scope to authorize access. To use Merchant API, your app must request the following scope on the OAuth consent screen: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/content Check the response from an OAuth request to verify that your app received this scope. See OAuth 2.0 policies for more details. Authorize requests Every request your application sends to the Merchant API must include an authorization token. The token also identifies your application to Google. About authorization protocols Your application must use OAuth 2.0 to authorize requests. No other authorization protocols are supported. If your application uses Sign In With Google , some aspects of authorization are handled for you. Authorizing requests with OAuth 2.0 All requests to the Merchant API must be authorized by an authenticated user. The details of the authorization process, or "flow," for OAuth 2.0 vary somewhat depending on what kind of application you're writing. The following general process applies to all application types: When you create your application, you register it using the Google API Console . Google then provides information you'll need later, such as a client ID and a client secret. Activate the Merchant API in the Google API Console. (If the API isn't listed in the API Console, then skip this step.) When your application needs access to user data, it asks Google for a particular scope of access. Google displays a consent screen to the user, asking them to authorize your application to request some of their data. If the user approves, then Google gives your application a short-lived access token . Your application requests user data, attaching the access token to the request. If Google determines that your request and the token are valid, it returns the requested data. Some flows include additional steps, such as using refresh tokens to acquire new access tokens. For detailed information about flows for various types of applications, see Google's OAuth 2.0 documentation . Here's the OAuth 2.0 scope information for the Merchant API: Scope Meaning https://www.googleapis.com/auth/content Read/write access. To request access using OAuth 2.0, your application needs the scope information, as well as information that Google supplies when you register your application (such as the client ID and the client secret). title: CatalogCanary – WordPress plugin | WordPress.org
text: CatalogCanary – WordPress plugin | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Plugin Directory CatalogCanary Submit a plugin My favorites Log in Submit a plugin My favorites Log in Search plugins CatalogCanary By canarylabs Download Details Reviews Development Support Description Most feed plugins generate a file and go quiet. When the feed breaks — products silently vanish, required fields go missing, a run hangs and never finishes — you find out weeks later when your ad performance craters. CatalogCanary treats the feed as something to guard , not just generate: Meta catalog feed (CSV) regenerated hourly, built in batches so large catalogs never time out, and published atomically — Meta never fetches a half-written file. Change monitoring — every run is compared against the last one. If your product count drops by more than your chosen threshold (10% by default) and you didn’t remove those products, you get an email immediately. Required-field checking — products that would be rejected by Meta (missing price, image, description…) are reported to you with the exact missing fields, not silently dropped. Variable products done properly — every variation becomes its own catalog item with its own price, image and link, grouped by item_group_id , with colour/size/material/pattern mapped to Meta’s variant fields. If a variable product ends up with no variations in the feed, that’s called out separately — it means the whole product has vanished from your catalog, which is easy to miss among per-variation warnings. Stuck-run watchdog — a separate check catches runs that started and never finished, so a dying cron can’t take your feed down quietly. A quiet admin screen — no review nags, no upsell banners, no dashboard spam. An alert history table and a Run Now button. Everything listed above is free, and nothing on this list is a trial or a teaser. There is a paid version, CatalogCanary Pro, which adds change diffs showing exactly which products left the feed and when, exclusion rules by category, tag, stock state, price or SKU, and webhook alerts into Slack. It is mentioned once, at the bottom of the plugin’s own settings page, and nowhere else in your admin. FAQ Where do I put the feed URL? Meta Commerce Manager → Catalog → Data sources → Scheduled feed. The URL is shown on the CatalogCanary page under WooCommerce in your admin. Which alerts are sent, and where? Email to your site admin address, or any address you set on the settings screen, when: a run fails, the product count drops by more than your threshold (10% by default) vs the previous run, products are skipped for missing required fields, or a run doesn’t finish within 6 hours. Every alert is also kept in an on-site log in case your email delivery is broken. Is my catalog exposed at a public URL? The feed filename contains a long random token generated on your site, so it cannot be guessed, and the folder is not browsable. You can regenerate the URL at any time from the settings screen — the old one stops working immediately, so remember to update it in Meta Commerce Manager. Does it support Google Shopping / TikTok / Pinterest? Not yet. CatalogCanary does one channel properly rather than 200 badly. Can I extend it? Yes. The plugin exposes catalogcanary_include_product and catalogcanary_product_data filters, and catalogcanary_run_finished and catalogcanary_alert actions. Everything the plugin advertises works without any add-on — nothing here is reserved or locked. Pro adds features that do not exist in this version; it does not switch on ones you already have. Reviews There are no reviews for this plugin. Contributors & Developers “CatalogCanary” is open source software. The following people have contributed to this plugin. Contributors canarylabs Translate “CatalogCanary” into your language. Interested in development? Browse the code , check out the SVN repository , or subscribe to the development log by RSS . Changelog 0.5.0 Added a single line at the foot of the CatalogCanary settings page noting that a paid version exists. No admin notices, no banners, nothing outside the plugin’s own screen, and no free feature was removed or gated to make room for it. 0.4.0 Added filters and actions so other plugins can exclude products, adjust feed data, react to a finished run, or deliver alerts elsewhere. No existing behaviour changes. 0.3.0 Settings screen: alert email, brand handling, and the drop-alert threshold are now configurable instead of fixed. Per-product brands. Reads WooCommerce’s brand taxonomy, a brand attribute, or a brand custom field, falling back to a brand you choose — previously every item was sent with the shop name, which is wrong for multi-brand stores. The feed URL now contains a random token, so nobody can guess it and download your whole catalog. It can be regenerated at any time. Added an uninstall routine that removes all options, scheduled jobs and generated files. 0.2.0 Variable product support: one feed row per variation, shared item_group_id , and Woo attributes mapped to Meta’s color/size/material/pattern fields. Variations inherit the parent’s image and description when they have none of their own, instead of failing validation. New alerts for variable products that contribute nothing to the catalog — either no variations exist, or every one failed validation. Alerts now name the product, not just its ID, and say which parent a failing variation belongs to. 0.1.0 Initial release: Meta CSV feed, batched generation, drop/missing-field/stuck alerts, admin status page. title: FAQs - Meta Business Extension - Documentation - Meta for Developers
text: FAQs - Meta Business Extension - Documentation - Meta for Developers Meta Business Extension Overview Partner Integrations Get Started Walkthroughs Integration Review Self-serve Testing Reference Direct Support Offsite Deprecation Changelog FAQs Meta Business Extension FAQs Answers to frequently asked questions about the Meta Business Extension (MBE) integration. Installation Why am I having trouble using channel: COMMERCE or channel: COMMERCE_OFFSITE? Commerce/Shops onboarding flows are currently only available to select partners in a closed beta. If you are interested in receiving access in the future, please contact your Facebook representative and review this document for reference. Permalink Why is the installed_features array missing on the fbe_installs endpoint for a particular merchant's external ID? Ensure that the merchant has MBE currently installed and has selected all applicable business assets during onboarding. Permalink In the Meta Business Extension Business Login flow, there is no screen to select a Catalog. Please make sure the 'Enable Catalog' checkbox is enabled under the Meta Business Extension Developer Panel > Setup tab in the App Dashboard. Permalink Can businesses/sellers update their Business Manager, Ad Account, Facebook Page, Meta Pixel, and Catalog in the Management View UI? Businesses/sellers can configure business features in the Management View, but will not be able to update Meta Business Extension connected Facebook assets such as Business Manager, Ad Account, Page, Pixel, Catalog, and so on. Alternatively, businesses/sellers can edit settings in the Meta Business Extension setup flow to connect with different assets. Permalink Which flow do I need? Depending on your business need, you may choose to set up one or more of the following flows by configuring the appropriate value under Setup > Channel : Default flow (no param required for channel) - Allows sellers to set up Metal Pixel, Facebook Page, Ad Account and Catalog for dynamic ads. COMMERCE — Flow that allows the sellers to create a commerce account with Facebook Shop and Instagram Shopping Channel with onsite. checkout. Also proves an option to choose offsite shops within the flow. COMMERCE_OFFSITE - Flow allowing sellers to create a Commerce Account with Offsite Facebook Shop and Offsite Instagram Shopping. FEED - Flow allowing retailers to sync their catalog updates. Recommended only for partners that have feed/catalog capabilities, and do not have website hosting. MARKETPLACE - Flow specific to marketplaces integrating with Meta Business Extension. Recommended for partners who only need the Page and Business Manager steps in the Meta Business Extension setup flow and then leverage Meta Business Extension Management View to set up Collaborative Ads. SIGNALS - Flow allows users to fire Meta Pixel and Conversions API events. This flow does not support Facebook Catalog as an asset. Recommended only for partners that have website hosting capabilities, and do not have catalog capabilities. Permalink During Meta Business Extension Business Login, what happens if the selected Page is currently owned by a Business Manager that is not the one selected in the flow? Below are some common scenarios you may encounter when selecting Facebook Pages during Meta Business Extension Business Login. Note that the tooltips in the Meta Business Extension flow will explain the exact reason why you are not able to select an asset -- the reason can differ from one scenario to another. A Facebook Page will be available for selection: If the selected Facebook Page is not owned by any Business Manager, the Facebook Page will be claimed by the selected Business Manager If the selected Facebook Page is owned by another Business Manager and is not a primary page of that BM, the Facebook Page will be transferred to the selected Business Manager A Facebook Page will not be available for selection: If a Facebook Page is owned by and is also a primary page of another Business Manager If a Facebook Page is owned by a BM which has been disabled, for example, for policy violations Permalink With the Page returned after Meta Business Extension installation, can a partner retrieve the Page’s public fields, for example, Page name, fan counts, link, picture, and so on? Partners can request the Page Public Metadata Access feature for their app, so that the app can query Page public fields. Learn more about this feature in this document and also here . Permalink Instagram profile IDs are not being returned via Meta Business Extension Installation API or Webhooks after Meta Business Extension is installed. If the instagram_profiles field is not included, this means Instagram-related permission (for example, instagram_basic ) is not included in the access token and/or the business has not connected any Instagram business profile with Meta Business Extension. For more on Meta Business Extension Installation API, see this document . Permalink Business Manager ID is not being returned via Meta Business Extension Installation API or Webhooks after Meta Business Extension install. This means some permission is missing in the app. Note that the main permission needed for Business Manager related actions is business_management . Permalink Which currencies does Meta Business Extension support? We support most of the currencies on this list except JMD, BGN, BYN, UAH, KIP, LKR, KYD. Warning: Meta Business Extension install will fail if non-supported currencies are provided in the extras setup settings. We recommend developers check that all their businesses are using supported currencies before allowing them to launch Meta Business Extension. Permalink I received an 'admin permission required' error during the onboarding flow. What do I do? Make sure you have admin access in the Meta Business Manager associated with the current Meta Business Extension connection, in addition to admin access to your Facebook business Page or Instagram Professional account. Follow these instructions on how to add an admin to your Meta Business Manager. Permalink Testing Can a test user on my app generate a system user access token? No, system user access tokens can't be generated for test users. Permalink How can a merchant remove connected assets (example: an Instagram account) from MBE? Merchants can remove assets in the management view of MBE after installation. Permalink Why am I not seeing the permissions I have selected in "scopes" in the FBE onboarding process for my merchants? Ensure that your app has been approved for "advanced access" for any permission you're using in the scopes of your business login URL, and that the permissions are “active” for your app. Permalink How can I test my app's FBE functionality? There are two types of test accounts available via the developer panel. Testers: Tester role can be assigned to a user-generated Facebook profile. Reference Test User: Test users are simulated Facebook user accounts. They cannot interact with real Facebook users. Reference Review each to decide which is better for your testing use case. Permalink Troubleshooting While troubleshooting merchant login issues, is it better to fully uninstall MBE, or to re-authorize with the previously connected assets? For troubleshooting, it's best to uninstall (with a DELETE request) and then re-install MBE for a particular merchant. Permalink What can a merchant do if they’re having a problem with the MBE onboarding flow? A good first step is uninstalling and then re-installing MBE. If they're still experiencing issues, they can reach out in the "Contact Us" link of MBE onboarding or the "Help Center" form on the MBE management view UI. Permalink General What do I need to do to get access to MBE? Your app must be whitelisted to have approval to use the Meta Business Extension. If you aren't approved for MBE, you'll encounter errors while trying to set up your MBE assets. Contact your partner manager to confirm that your app has been whitelisted for MBE. Permalink Where can I go for help on an MBE alpha/beta product that isn't currently available to all MBE partners? Please reach out to your partner manager or engineering contact. Permalink How do I get access to a Commerce channel for MBE? This is a closed beta. Please reach out to your Meta partner manager for more information. Permalink Catalog What is Catalog and why do I need it? The Facebook Business Extension (FBE) v2 uses Catalog to intake a business's inventory. It is used to power various features, such as Dynamic Ads, Shops, and Page services card. It is an optional part of the integration, but is required for those features. See FBE Catalog API documentation for implementation details and supported fields. Permalink How can I get access to the Catalog API? Your app will need to get approved Catalog permission ( catalog_management ) via App Review before going live. Add catalog_management permission to the scope parameter in your Business Login implementation, it will allow your app to create, read, update and delete business-owned catalogs. Submit an App Review request as soon as you have a working demo you can use to screencast how: Catalog permission is requested on the onboarding flow The inventory is pushed to the connected Catalog The Catalog-powered features are enabled after the Catalog was synced Permalink I have been rejected for the Catalog API. What do I do? Our App Review team will use the instructions and screencast you provide to test and verify your app's Facebook integration for Catalog. If you got a rejection, please make sure to read through the provided feedback to understand the reason. You should resubmit for review with updated information that provides more details for the reviewer. Please visit our App Review Rejection Results Guide for tips on how to have a successful App Review and how to notify your Meta partner manager about your rejections for further assistance Permalink Why is my catalog not eligible in the onboarding flow? Asset selection is interlinked and has multiple reasons to fail eligibility. Some of the reasons could be: Your selected page is already linked with a different catalog Your catalog is associated with a different commerce account If your catalog is used with the test app and you cannot use the same catalog for production Permalink Migration In FBE 1.0, a Page can only be connected to one partner platform. In FBE 2.0, can businesses/sellers connect a profile, that is, a Facebook Page or Instagram business profile, to multiple partner platforms? In FBE 2.0, a Facebook Page or Instagram business profile can be connected to more than one partner platform (based on App ID). However, the same profile can only be connected once for a given partner platform. Permalink Will Messenger chat and Page Shop migrate automatically when we migrate FBE from the old to the new version? No. For Messenger chat, partner platforms can enable it by setting the messenger_chat of business_config in Business Login. For Page Shop, businesses/sellers have to enable it in the Management View after migration. Permalink Where can I go for help on multi-feature use cases in MBE 3.0? There is a guide to migrate from MBE 2.0 to 3.0 in our documentation, but you can reach out to your Meta partner manager or engineering contact with specific questions. Permalink Plugins Are the Instagram Shopping and Page Shop plugins still supported in FBE Management View? No. These two plugins are now deprecated from FBE management view. Messenger Chat is the only plugin supported as of 2021. Permalink For the 'messenger_chat' feature setup via Business Login, do partners need to validate the URLs of the 'domains' field? HTTPS is required for Messenger allowlisted domains. Partners should validate the domains field URLs with protocol ID, that is, https:// Learn more about how to configure the FBEMessengerChatConfigData object. Permalink For the `messenger_chat` feature setup via Business Login, can the partner platforms set the `domains` field and leave it to the businesses/sellers to enable `messenger_chat` after FBE setup? Partners may be in a better position to ensure the Messenger domain is valid and remove the hassle for businesses/sellers to set up the domains. Partners can set messenger_chat.domains in the business_config of FBE Business Login and set messenger_chat.enabled=false Businesses/sellers can later enable Messenger plugin in Management View or partners can provide a way for the businesses/sellers to do it on their platforms via Feature Configuration API. Permalink Integration Review What is Integration Review? Integration Review is the process where Facebook verifies your FBE integration. Once your app's Integration Review is successful, your app will be available to public users (that is, business users and sellers). You can request integration review in the Integration Review tab in your app's FBE Developer Panel after all requirements are implemented. To help expedite the review process, you should also share with our reviewers or your FB representative an end-to-end working demo video of all the FBE features you have implemented. Only administrators and developers of your app will be able to initiate the FBE flow until your app has successfully completed review. See more details about FBE Developer Panel limitations Permalink Where can I go for help on my integration review? Please reach out to your Meta partner manager, or submit a new integration review. Permalink SDK / API / Webhooks / Mobile Is Facebook Business Extension supported on mobile devices? Yes, FBE is supported on m-browsers and can also be launched using Webviews through your native Android / iOS application. Learn more about launching FBE in mobile . Permalink How can I get the access_token to call the Feature Configuration API after Management View is dismissed? Access tokens are required to make Graph API calls. The different types of access tokens are explained here . You may call Facebook Login to get the access_token before launching Management View, and then use that access_token to call the Feature Configuration API . Sample code: function launchFBEManagementView(access_token) { FB.ui({ display: 'popup', method: 'facebook_business_extension', external_business_id: , }, function(response){ // call Feature Configuration API with access_token here }); } FB.getLoginStatus(function(response) { if (response.status === 'connected') { // returns a User Access Token with scopes requested access_token = response.authResponse.accessToken; // launch Management View launchFBEManagementView(access_token); } else { FB.login(function (response) { if (response.authResponse) { // returns a User Access Token with scopes requested access_token = response.authResponse.accessToken; // launch Management View launchFBEManagementView(access_token); } else { console.log('User cancelled login or did not fully authorize.'); } }, {}); } }); Permalink Shops Why is my Instagram business account not eligible for shops? To use Instagram Shopping for offsite or onsite flows, an Instagram business account is required. A personal Instagram account is not eligible. If your Instagram business account does not have an established presence or is not selling eligible goods, your account may not be eligible and you can request for re-verification in six (6) months. Please see the eligibility requirements . Permalink How can I set up both offsite and onsite shops? A commerce account can have either offsite shops or onsite shops. You can also convert onsite shops to offsite shops and vice versa. If your business needs both offsite and onsite shops, you will require two onboarding flows with different assets. Permalink Why is my page not eligible? Asset selection is interlinked and has multiple reasons to fail eligibility. Some of the reasons include: User is not an admin of the business that owns the Page Page is associated with a different Business Manager Permalink Contact Us I am a developer experiencing issues with Meta Business Extension. How can I report it and get help? Use the Direct Support tool in Business Manager to get assistance directly from our team: Commerce partners: use the topic Marketing Partner: Technical Support or contact your Meta Partner directly. If you don’t see your desired topic in the Direct Support dropdown menu, please contact your Meta Partner via email for access. Direct Support has a strong integration with Business Manager. So make sure to add all your team members who will be using the Direct Support tool to submit questions and bugs as users of your company Business Manager. Learn how to do this by following the instructions here . Permalink My merchant is experiencing issues with FBE. How can they get help? Throughout the FBE onboarding UI there is a “Having an Issue? Contact Us” link at the bottom of the page. Merchants should use this link to get FBE support. Permalink -->

One or more product feeds on your …… failed to generate. Please check the status of your feeds and try to manually regenerate them again. title: Catalog Currency Sync Issue: Products displaying in USD despite Store/Catalog be | WordPress.org
text: Catalog Currency Sync Issue: Products displaying in USD despite Store/Catalog be | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Meta for WooCommerce / Catalog Currency Sync Issue: Products displaying in USD despite Store/Catalog be Search for: Search forums Catalog Currency Sync Issue: Products displaying in USD despite Store/Catalog be Resolved zenha2022 (@zenha2022) 4 months ago Hi Support Team, I am currently experiencing a persistent issue with my Meta for WooCommerce integration. My store is based in Portugal and configured to use EUR as the default currency. My Meta Commerce Manager catalog is also correctly set to EUR . However, most of my products are appearing in the Facebook Catalog with the currency set to USD . The situation: My WooCommerce settings are correctly set to EUR. The Commerce Manager catalog default currency is set to EUR. Despite this, the products in the catalog are showing up in USD. The only way I have found to fix this is by manually editing each product in the Commerce Manager, which is not sustainable. Technical details & previous issues: I am currently using a filter to explicitly force the currency to ‘EUR’ and to format the price in the facebook_for_woocommerce_integration_prepare_product hook. Even with this code in place, the Facebook catalog seems to ignore the value or is using a cached/locked currency value from a previous sync. Additionally, I previously faced major issues with decimal formatting—my store is configured to use dots (.) for decimals, but the Facebook integration was interpreting values incorrectly (e.g., 165€ appearing as 1.65€). I had to force the formatting in my functions.php to ensure the API received the correct float format (165.00) without relying on local server settings. PHP // My current filter: add_filter( 'facebook_for_woocommerce_integration_prepare_product', 'b2bking_fix_facebook_price_currency', 10, 2 ); function b2bking_fix_facebook_price_currency( $product_data, $product_id ) { $product = wc_get_product( $product_id ); if ( $product ) { $price_to_use = !empty( $product->get_sale_price() ) ? $product->get_sale_price() : $product->get_regular_price(); // Forcing format to 165.00 $product_data['price'] = number_format( (float) $price_to_use, 2, '.', '' ); // Forcing currency $product_data['currency'] = 'EUR'; } return $product_data; } It seems like the Meta plugin is either not updating the currency field for existing products or is defaulting to a historical currency preference. My questions: Is there a way to force a full re-sync of all product metadata, including currency, without having to delete the entire catalog? Is there a specific filter I should be using for the “Meta for WooCommerce” plugin to ensure the currency is overwritten for existing items? Why would the plugin be overriding my store’s currency settings even when the catalog is set to EUR? I would appreciate any guidance on how to fix this for all products at once, as the current manual overhead is significant. Best regards, Miguel The page I need help with: [ log in to see the link] Viewing 3 replies - 1 through 3 (of 3 total) Plugin Support Marija (@marijastuntcoders) 4 months ago Hi @zenha2022 , thank you for reaching out! Can you try the following: Go to Commerce Manager > Data Sources > [Pixel name] > Settings > Default currency and check if it’s set to EUR. Remove/comment out any custom code you have added to override the plugin’s behaviour Temporarily disable any cache plugins on your site, and clear the cache Go to Marketing > Facebook > Product Sync and run the manual sync from here The products in the Commerce Manager should display the correct currency If the issue persists, please share the following using PasteBin : System Status report The latest facebook_for_woocommerce log (located in WooCommerce > Status > Logs) Any plugin-related errors from your debug.log A link and screenshots for a product you are still having issues with (where the currency is set to EUR , but is displayed as USD ). Kind regards, Marija Plugin Support Marija (@marijastuntcoders) 3 months, 3 weeks ago Hi @zenha2022 , Just wanted to follow up and check if you are still experiencing this issue? If so, please share the following using PasteBin : System Status report The latest facebook_for_woocommerce log (located in WooCommerce > Status > Logs) Any plugin-related errors from your debug.log A link and screenshots for a product you are still having issues with (where the currency is set to EUR , but is displayed as USD ) Kind regards, Marija Plugin Support Marija (@marijastuntcoders) 3 months, 3 weeks ago Hi @zenha2022 , Since we haven’t heard back from you in a while, we will be marking this issue as resolved. Please feel free to reach out again if you need any further assitance. Kind regards, Marija Viewing 3 replies - 1 through 3 (of 3 total) You must be logged in to reply to this topic. title: Category filter results in an empty XML feed while unfiltered feed works | WordPress.org
text: Category filter results in an empty XML feed while unfiltered feed works | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce by AdTribes – Product Feeds for WooCommerce / Category filter results in an empty XML feed while unfiltered feed works Search for: Search forums Category filter results in an empty XML feed while unfiltered feed works Resolved cloturearesdigital (@cloturearesdigital) 3 weeks, 5 days ago Hi, I’m experiencing an issue with category filters in Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce (Free). Environment: WordPress 7.1.1 WooCommerce 10.9.4 Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce 13.5.7 PHP 8.3 Feed: Google Shopping / XML The feed works correctly when no filters are applied : products and variations are generated in the XML. However, as soon as I add an Include filter such as: Category → Contains → Barreaudage tubes ronds the generated XML becomes completely empty (no entries). I tested the parent category and several child categories, with the same result. The category definitely contains products. For example, one of the products is a standard WooCommerce variable product directly assigned to: Barreaudage (parent) Barreaudage tubes ronds (child) Its variations are enabled, priced, in stock and purchasable. The System Check correctly detects the catalog ( 94 simple products + 544 variations = 638 products ) and correctly recognizes the WooCommerce category “Barreaudage tubes ronds” (category ID 366) . Regards, Laure Plugin Support Tanjir Al Mamun (@tanjiralmamun) 3 weeks, 4 days ago Hi @cloturearesdigital , Those reports are safe to post here, they hold no passwords or customer data. Your filter is set up correctly. The plugin stores a category filter by its slug, so barreaudage-tubes-ronds is exactly what it compares against. Your report also shows one run of this feed writing 48 items, and later runs of the same feed writing 0, and a filter that matched nothing would give 0 every time. So, the likely cause is how 13.5.7 pages through products between batches, not the filter. There is a confirmed defect there that can skip a whole block of products in a run. Unfiltered, that goes unnoticed among 600 items. Filtered down to a few dozen products sitting in the skipped block, you get an empty file. The fix ships in the next release. To confirm it, generate everything in one batch so there is no paging: Go to Product Feed → Settings → General . Tick “Change products per batch number” and set “ Insert batch size:” to 1000. Save, then go to Product Feed → Manage Feeds and run “Refresh Feed” on the filtered feed. If the products come back, that is it, and you can leave that setting on until the next release. If the feed is still empty, tick “Enable logging” on the same page, refresh once more, then open WooCommerce → Status → Logs and post the “Product Feed File Counted” entries from p roduct-feed-pro-by-adtribes-io . Cheers! Thread Starter cloturearesdigital (@cloturearesdigital) 3 weeks, 4 days ago Hi, thanks for your help! I enabled “Change products per batch number” and set the batch size to 1000, then saved the setting and manually refreshed the filtered feed. Unfortunately, the XML feed is still empty (no entries). I then enabled logging as requested and refreshed the feed again. The log shows: products_count => 638 processed_count => 638 and the feed generation is reported as completed successfully. However, the resulting XML is still empty. Also, there are no “Product Feed File Counted” entries in the generated product-feed-pro-by-adtribes-io log. The log only contains the “Product Feed Generation Started” and “Product Feed Generation Completed” entries. So it seems all 638 products are being processed in one batch, but none of the filtered products are being written to the XML. I can post the full log here if useful. Thanks! Plugin Support Tanjir Al Mamun (@tanjiralmamun) 3 weeks, 3 days ago Hi @cloturearesdigital , Thanks for running that. Batch size is ruled out: all 638 products went through in one batch, and the file is still empty, so paging is not what is losing them. The Product Feed File Counted line was my mistake. That entry only exists in a newer build than 13.5.7, so there was nothing there for you to find. I checked the filter mechanism itself against a matching setup: a variable product in a category with the same Category → Contains filter, and it picked out exactly the right variations. So I do not think the filter is misreading your setting. Looking at your shop, Barreaudage tubes ronds holds 3 products with 30 variations each, so a working filtered feed should come out to around 90 items. That gives us a clean test: Remove the category filter, refresh the feed once, then open the XML. Search for Panneau barreaudage à tubes ronds non traversants . If that product is missing from the unfiltered file too, the filter isn’t what is dropping it, and the cause sits further upstream. Tell me, and I will take it from there. If it is in there, then it is something about how the filter value is stored on your feed, and I will dig into that next. No need to post the full log for now. You can also untick Change products per batch number again. It is not doing anything here. Cheers! Thread Starter cloturearesdigital (@cloturearesdigital) 3 weeks, 3 days ago Hi, I ran the test and this seems to reveal the actual issue. I completely removed the category filter, saved the feed and refreshed it. “Panneau barreaudage à tubes ronds non traversants” is NOT present in the unfiltered XML either. I checked several other products and noticed a pattern: Barreaudage products are missing “PB gates” products are missing Accessories are present Some “sur mesure” products are present Some sectional doors are present So it now looks like the category filter itself is not causing these products to disappear. They are already being excluded somewhere upstream during feed generation, even with no filters applied. This would also explain why filtering by the Barreaudage category resulted in an empty feed. The Barreaudage products are standard WooCommerce variable products with enabled, priced and purchasable variations. For example, the product we previously checked has 30 WooCommerce variations. Could you please advise what Product Feed PRO checks before a product/variation is included in the feed, and what could cause these products to be skipped while accessories and some other products are exported? I can provide screenshots/settings for one working product and one missing product if that helps. Thanks! Plugin Support Tanjir Al Mamun (@tanjiralmamun) 3 weeks, 3 days ago Hi @cloturearesdigital , Thanks for the detailed follow-up. That’s exactly the kind of pattern that helps track this down. The batch size test was actually useful: increasing it to 1000 didn’t help because this isn’t a batch-sizing problem. It’s a defect in 13.5.7’s batch processing logic itself that can silently skip whole blocks of products no matter how the batches are sized. That fits everything you’re seeing: the item count changing between runs, specific categories missing from the unfiltered feed, and the filtered feed coming back empty since it draws from the same process. A fix for this is already built and going through testing before public release, so it isn’t out yet. In the meantime, I suggest you roll back to version 13.5.6, which predates this issue: Download the 13.5.6 from this link . Go to Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin , Upload the 13.5.6 zip Click Replace current with uploaded when WordPress offers it. Your settings and existing feeds stay as they are. Only the plugin files change, and WordPress keeps an automatic backup of the version being replaced. We’ll post an update here once the fix is out publicly. If 13.5.6 still leaves products missing, let us know, and we’ll keep digging. Cheers! Thread Starter cloturearesdigital (@cloturearesdigital) 3 weeks, 3 days ago Hi, I rolled back to version 13.5.6 as suggested and refreshed the feed. Unfortunately, the issue remains. Just to clarify, the feed currently has no category filter at all . I had already removed the filter for the previous test and kept it removed when testing 13.5.6. After refreshing the unfiltered feed on 13.5.6, “Panneau barreaudage à tubes ronds non traversants” is still missing from the XML , as are the other products I previously checked. So the products appear to be excluded upstream even on 13.5.6, before any category filtering is involved. I should also mention that I recently installed Product Feed PRO on another WooCommerce e-commerce website , where I am using version 13.5.7 , and I have not encountered this issue there. Products and category filters are working correctly on that website. This makes me wonder whether there may be something specific to this website, its product configuration, or its WooCommerce setup that is causing certain products/variations to be skipped. What would you recommend checking next? Thanks! Plugin Support Jeff Alvarez (@superlemon1998) 3 weeks, 2 days ago Hi @cloturearesdigital , Can you please confirm if you’ve already done a basic debug to check for any plugin or theme conflicts? You can quickly do this by disabling all plugins except WooCommerce and Product Feed Pro and only have Storefront theme(no customizations) You mentioned that it works on your other websites so it’s likely not a configuration error. So we are clear the issue you are facing is that products under certain categories aren’t showing on the XML file with no Filters/Rules active? Thread Starter cloturearesdigital (@cloturearesdigital) 3 weeks, 1 day ago Hi Jeff, Yes, that is correct: products from certain categories are missing from the XML feed even when no Filters or Rules are active . I haven’t performed the full plugin/theme conflict test yet. However, there is an important point regarding my other WooCommerce website where Product Feed PRO works correctly: the setup is essentially the same on both websites, including the same active plugins . On that other website, Product Feed PRO 13.5.7 correctly exports the products and the Category → Contains filters also work as expected. So, although I understand that a plugin or theme conflict still needs to be ruled out properly, there isn’t an obvious difference in the active plugin configuration between the working website and the affected one. I can run the test you suggested on a staging environment by disabling all plugins except WooCommerce and Product Feed PRO and temporarily switching to Storefront. And just to confirm the issue precisely: with no Filters/Rules active , the XML feed contains some products (mainly accessories and some custom-made products), while entire groups of other products are missing, including Barreaudage products and several variable gate products. Thanks! Plugin Support Jeff Alvarez (@superlemon1998) 2 weeks, 6 days ago Hi @cloturearesdigital , Could you please check if you have this option enabled to enforce the 500×500 image in Product Feed > Settings : https://ibb.co/YFbynqnF If enabled, please temporarily disable it and refresh the feed. View the feed via incognito and see if the products are now showing fine. Thread Starter cloturearesdigital (@cloturearesdigital) 2 weeks, 6 days ago Hi Jeff, I checked the setting you mentioned. “Enforce minimum 500×500 image size on Google Shopping and Facebook Catalog feeds” is already disabled on the affected website, so unfortunately this does not seem to be the cause. The issue therefore remains the same: with no Filters or Rules active , some products are exported correctly, while entire groups of products — including the Barreaudage variable products — are missing from the XML. Please let me know what you would like me to check next. Thanks! Thread Starter cloturearesdigital (@cloturearesdigital) 2 weeks, 5 days ago Hi Jeff, I found the cause of the issue. After performing the plugin conflict test on staging, I identified Product Filter for WooCommerce by WBW as the conflicting plugin. I confirmed it with an A/B test: WBW enabled → the affected products disappear from the XML feed WBW disabled → the products are correctly included again I then checked the production website and realized that this plugin was actually not being used anymore , even though it was still active. I have now disabled it on production, refreshed the Product Feed PRO feed, and everything is working correctly . The previously missing products are now present in the XML feed. So the issue is resolved on my side. I just wanted to let you know that there seems to be a compatibility issue between Product Feed PRO and Product Filter for WooCommerce by WBW , in case this is useful for your team. Thanks a lot for your help and Tanjir’s, and for taking the time to troubleshoot this with me! Have a good day! text: ChatGPT (OpenAI) Feed – CSV formatting and field value issues causing products t | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Product Feed Manager for WooCommerce – CTX Feed – Support 220+ Shopping, AI & Social Channels / ChatGPT (OpenAI) Feed – CSV formatting and field value issues causing products t Search for: Search forums ChatGPT (OpenAI) Feed – CSV formatting and field value issues causing products t Resolved razvan199 (@razvan199) 1 month, 1 week ago Hi, I’m having an issue with a product feed generated using the ChatGPT (OpenAI) template in CTX Feed for WooCommerce. I’m using: Template: ChatGPT (OpenAI) File Type: CSV Delimiter: Comma Enclosure: " Include Variations: All Variations Country: Romania The main mappings are generated using the ChatGPT/OpenAI template. One issue I found is the Availability output. CTX generates: in stock while the OpenAI specification expects: in_stock Similarly, WooCommerce _stock_status cannot be used directly because values such as: instock outofstock onbackorder also do not match the OpenAI values: in_stock out_of_stock backorder Manual feed test To determine whether the problem was related to CTX’s output or to the products themselves, I manually reformatted the feed according to the OpenAI feed specification. I converted it to a Google-compatible structure: id title description link image_link availability price brand identifier_exists I also made the following changes: in stock → in_stock Descriptions were cleaned and limited to 5,000 characters. I removed one product that had no image URL. I also ensured the CSV used standard double-quote enclosure and valid UTF-8 encoding. After this change, OpenAI stopped reporting the original formatting errors. There was initially one remaining issue with price . CTX was generating prices above 1,000 RON like: 1,099.90 RON 1,389.90 RON 1,999.00 RON OpenAI rejected those values. After manually changing them to: 1099.90 RON 1389.90 RON 1999.00 RON the feed uploaded without any misformatted-column errors .Current result The manually corrected file contains 1,237 products . OpenAI currently reports: Ingested: 622 Processed: 622 Rejected: 48 Ready: 574 So this is by far the most successful upload so far, and there are no longer any “Misformatted columns” errors . The remaining difference between the 1,237 rows in the CSV and the 622 products ingested by OpenAI is something I’m still investigating and may be related to OpenAI’s ingestion/eligibility process rather than CTX. However, the manual test seems to confirm that at least some of the original issues are related to the output generated by the CTX ChatGPT (OpenAI) template. Could you please check whether the current ChatGPT/OpenAI template in CTX Feed is fully aligned with the latest OpenAI product feed specification, particularly regarding: Availability values CTX output: in stock Expected OpenAI output: in_stock Price formatting CTX can output: 1,099.90 RON while OpenAI appears to require: 1099.90 RON CSV formatting/enclosure , especially for long product descriptions containing commas and line breaks. Whether the CTX ChatGPT (OpenAI) template should currently generate the native OpenAI schema ( item_id , url , image_url , etc.) or the Google-compatible schema ( id , link , image_link , etc.). Whether there are any recommended CTX settings, Dynamic Attributes, or String Replace rules specifically required for OpenAI feeds. Thanks! Viewing 8 replies - 1 through 8 (of 8 total) Plugin Support mansary (@mansary) 1 month, 1 week ago Hi, Thank you for the detailed report and for performing the manual feed test. We reviewed the issues against the latest CTX Feed version. Please update CTX Feed to the latest version, 8.0.18 , and regenerate the feed before testing again. 1. Availability The ChatGPT (OpenAI) template in CTX Feed already converts availability values such as instock and in stock to the OpenAI-compatible in_stock format. Please update the plugin to version 8.0.18 , make sure the feed is using the ChatGPT (OpenAI) template, and regenerate the feed. Then check whether the availability values are generated correctly. 2. Backorder / Pre-order We also fixed an issue in older versions where certain backorder/pre-order products could be generated with an incorrect value. This has been addressed in version 8.0.18 . 3. Price formatting The comma in prices such as 1,099.90 RON is coming from the WooCommerce number format settings . CTX Feed uses the WooCommerce-configured number formatting for the product price. Overriding the number format directly within the feed is not available in the free version of CTX Feed. If the OpenAI feed requires the price without a thousand separator, you would need to adjust the relevant WooCommerce number formatting settings or use the available Pro functionality. 4. OpenAI schema The ChatGPT (OpenAI) template is designed to use the supported OpenAI feed structure. Fields such as id , link , and image_link are valid, so there is no need to switch to a Google template or manually rename these fields to item_id , url , image_url , etc. 5. CSV formatting and descriptions CTX Feed uses the configured CSV enclosure and handles values containing commas appropriately. For long descriptions, we recommend keeping the content clean and avoiding unnecessary HTML or unsupported characters. No additional String Replace rules should normally be required for availability when using the ChatGPT (OpenAI) template. Please first update CTX Feed to 8.0.18 , regenerate the feed, and check the output again. If you still see any formatting issues after the update, please send us the newly generated feed URL and we will investigate further. The error that I receive when I use the product feed link is the following: “Misformatted columns Following columns were misformatted in the last upload price 1,277 rows affected” Looks like the only issue now is the “price” column. This is the newly regenerated feed URL after I updated the pluggin to version 8.0.18: https://discoverbeauty.ro/wp-content/uploads/woo-feed/chatgpt/csv/gptfeed.csv Thank you Plugin Support mansary (@mansary) 1 month ago Hi @razvan199 Thank you for the detailed follow-up and for sharing the feed URL — that let us pinpoint the exact cause. We downloaded your current gptfeed.csv and checked every price row. The good news first: the thousands-separator problem is gone (prices over 1,000 now export as 1099.90 with no comma), and your availability values are all correctly in_stock. Those two issues are resolved. The remaining “price — misformatted columns” error is something else, and it affects every row, which is why OpenAI reports ~1,277 rows: the currency code is glued to the number with no space. Your feed currently ships 1099.90RON, 35.90RON, etc., while OpenAI requires the standard money format 1099.90 RON (number, space, ISO currency code). This is a confirmed bug in CTX Feed versions 8.0.14 through 8.0.18 — feeds configured before 8.0.14 could lose the leading space in front of the currency code — and it was fixed in version 8.0.19. You are currently on 8.0.18, which is why it still appears. What to do: Update CTX Feed to the latest version (8.0.21 as of today). Regenerate the ChatGPT (OpenAI) feed. No settings changes and no feed re-creation are needed — the fix applies automatically on the next generation. Re-upload to OpenAI. Prices will now ship as 1099.90 RON. One more improvement worth mentioning: since 8.0.19, feed prices default to the clean machine format — exactly two decimals, dot separator, no thousands grouping — independently of your WooCommerce display settings, and ChatGPT (OpenAI) feeds additionally strip any grouping commas OpenAI rejects. So you no longer need to adjust WooCommerce’s number formatting for the feed’s sake; I’d like to correct our earlier note on that point — this now works out of the box in the free version. On the earlier ingested-vs-total gap (622 of 1,237): once the price format is fixed and the file re-uploaded, that number should improve. Any remaining rejections at that point would be per-product data requirements on OpenAI’s side (for example, products without an image, like the one you removed manually). If a gap persists after the update, share the new numbers and we’ll dig into those rows with you. Thank you again for the careful testing — your manual experiment isolated the problem beautifully. I contacted support and they just suggested I try again without filters (Ummm, I did that before I contacted you!). I replied that I had tried that without success. What changed about the attribute dropdown In a recent release we tightened up the Field Mapping picker so WooCommerce global attributes (the pa_* taxonomy attributes) only appear in one group instead of two. Previously they showed up under both “Added Custom Attributes” and “Dynamic attributes”, which led to a lot of “which one do I pick?” confusion. They now live exclusively under “Dynamic attributes” . That’s why pa packaging / pa_opakowanie doesn’t appear under “Added Custom Attributes” anymore. What you should select Looking at your screenshots, “Opakowanie” is set up as a WooCommerce global attribute (your Products > Attributes screen confirms it — slug opakowanie , taxonomy pa_opakowanie ). For a global attribute, the correct choice in Field Mapping is: Dynamic attributes > Product Opakowanie Not the “Opakowanie” entry under Added Custom Attributes — that one matches an unrelated post-meta key (likely from another plugin), not the taxonomy term assigned to your product. That’s why your feed was coming through without the packaging value. Switch the mapping for ilosc_sztuk_w_opak to “Product Opakowanie” under Dynamic attributes, save, and re-export. The feed should pick up the value (15 in your test product) again. About the CSV feed showing “Error” That’s still worth a closer look. Could you also send a debug log so we can see what’s failing? Steps here: https://adtribes.io/knowledge-base/send-your-debug-log-to-support/ Plus, briefly: Open the feed inside Manage Feeds and check for an inline error message Or open the feed URL in the browser and paste the message that appears Roughly how many products are included in this feed? Two recent CSV-feed fixes shipped around the same time (an empty-batch handling bug and a multi-value separator fix). text: Feed stuck | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce by AdTribes – Product Feeds for WooCommerce / Feed stuck Search for: Search forums Feed stuck Resolved ianatkins (@ianatkins) 5 months, 1 week ago Hello. Feed has stuck and been silently failing to build for days. In the logs I just see multiple starting entries. Scheduled actions are setup to run via CLI and CRON, so are running without issue. I enabled ‘Disable HTTP feed generation requests’ and set the batch size to 500, and regenerated the feed, but is now stuck at 90%. No errors logged, but log entries everyday for when it runs. Running WooCommerce 10.5.2, Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce 13.5.4 Thanks. Ian 2026-05-13T11:05:28+00:00 Debug Product Feed Memory Usage: Array ( [feed_id] => 34237 [label] => Batch start [offset] => 1000 [batch_size] => 500 [memory_current] => 27 MB [memory_real] => 30 MB [memory_peak] => 30 MB [memory_limit] => 512M ) 2026-05-13T01:35:10+00:00 Info Product Feed Generation Started: Array ( [feed_id] => 34237 [feed_title] => Facebook Feed [execution_date] => 2026-05-13 02:35:10 [context] => schedule [channel] => Array ( [channel_hash] => d4cb75caae5a73ac6b01171816b33bfb [name] => Google Shopping [fields] => google_shopping [taxonomy] => google_shopping [utm_source] => Google Shopping [type] => Advertising ) [file_format] => xml [action] => Feed generation started ) CONTEXT: {"_legacy":true} Viewing 1 replies (of 1 total) Plugin Support Jeff Alvarez (@superlemon1998) 5 months ago Hi @ianatkins , Can you please check if you have any failed scheduled actions or any critical errors? Also, you mentioned that it’s stuck at 90%, can you try lowering your batch size and see if that fixes things. If not, try creating a new feed and see if that helps with stability. There can be cases where simply manually refreshing or creating a new feed fixes things. And if you haven’t yet, run a basic debug to confirm that it isn’t a plugin or theme conflict.
