The Product Feed page is not loading the Overview Stats and displays the following message: “There was an error loading the Overview Stats. The scheduled job has been paused due to a high failure rate.” All products are currently displayed as “Not synced”. Under WooCommerce → Status → Scheduled Actions, the following hook has accumulated approximately 390 failed actions: gla/jobs/update_merchant_product_statuses/process_item The failed actions contain this error: MerchantStatuses::parse_presync_issue_text(): Argument #1 ($text) must be of type string, array given, called in MerchantStatuses.php on line 613. The actions start correctly through WP-Cron but fail after the TypeError. The job is then stopped because its failure rate is above the allowed threshold. Could you please advise how to fix or safely reset this job without losing the current Google Merchant Center and Google Ads connections? I have not rerun or deleted the failed actions, and I have not disconnected the linked Google accounts. Thank you. The page I need help with: [ log in to see the link] Viewing 11 replies - 1 through 11 (of 11 total) shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi @sbentes ! Thank you for reaching out and providing the details. From your description, I understand that the Overview Stats on the Google for WooCommerce Product Feed page are failing to load, the scheduled job has been paused due to a high failure rate, and all of your products are currently showing as Not synced . To help us narrow down the cause, could you please let us know if you made any changes to your site before this issue started occurring? For example, did you recently update WordPress, WooCommerce, the Google for WooCommerce plugin, your theme, or any other plugins? Additionally, could you please share the following: Your System Status Report from WooCommerce → Status . Any relevant fatal error logs from WooCommerce → Status → Logs (please check for logs related to Google for WooCommerce or any recent fatal errors). You can share both using Pastebin. If possible, please enable the “Burn after read” option before sharing the link. Once we have that information, we’ll be happy to investigate further. Thread Starter sbentes (@sbentes) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi, Thank you for your reply. I cannot identify a specific change made immediately before the issue started. The first failures currently visible in Action Scheduler date from May 20, 2026. The site has received routine WordPress, WooCommerce, theme, and plugin updates, but I did not intentionally disconnect or reconnect the Merchant Center or Google Ads accounts. Google for WooCommerce is currently version 3.8.1. I recently performed database maintenance, but this was after the Google for WooCommerce issue had already started. I deliberately did not delete any failed or pending GLA actions, modify GLA tables, or change the existing Google connection. System Status Report: https://pastebin.com/jFZiDVbF Relevant error logs: https://pastebin.com/S5n0cRgp https://pastebin.com/Nn5Q9tmA The recurring Action Scheduler error is: Automattic\WooCommerce\GoogleListingsAndAds\MerchantCenter\MerchantStatuses::parse_presync_issue_text(): Argument #1 ($text) must be of type string, array given, called in MerchantStatuses.php on line 613. The hook gla/jobs/update_merchant_product_statuses/process_item accumulated approximately 390 failed actions and was paused after exceeding the allowed failure threshold. The Product Feed Overview Stats do not load, and the products are shown as “Not synced.” Please let me know the safest way to repair or restart this job without losing the current Merchant Center and Google Ads connections. Thank you. shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi @sbentes ! Thank you for sharing the logs and the System Status Report. I tried to review the System Status Report, but it appears that the link contains the error logs instead of the actual System Status Report. Could you please share the System Status Report again? You can find it by navigating to WooCommerce → Status , then copy the report and share it with us via Pastebin. I also reviewed the logs you shared. The Google for WooCommerce and WP Desk Sender logs are DEBUG logs, which indicate normal background activity rather than errors. The Google for WooCommerce logs show that the plugin is synchronizing products with Google Merchant Center, while the WP Desk Sender logs show that the plugin is sending diagnostic information about your store. Based on the logs you’ve shared, I don’t see any ERROR or CRITICAL entries that would indicate a problem. Once you share the correct System Status Report, I’ll be happy to take a closer look and continue investigating the issue. Thread Starter sbentes (@sbentes) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi, Thank you. Here is the correct WooCommerce System Status Report: https://pastebin.com/CuNs313c Please let me know if you need any additional information. Thank you. shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi @sbentes ! Thank you for sharing the System Status Report. I had a chance to review it, and everything appears to be in order. Could you please update Google for WooCommerce to the latest version? In the latest release, we’ve included a fix related to verifying the data source during Merchant API product sync , which may be related to the issue you’re experiencing. After updating the plugin, Please navigate to this setting: example.com/wp-admin/admin.php?page=connection-test-admin-page ( making sure to replace example.com with your own domain ). Head to the product sync section at the bottom and click Sync All Products with Google Merchant Center That will sync all your products to GMC or it can return an error at the top of the page, if there is an error please let us know. If you can share a screenshot of the error, that would be great! Let me know how that goes. Thread Starter sbentes (@sbentes) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi, I updated Google for WooCommerce and ran “Sync All Products with Google Merchant Center” from the connection test page, as requested. The result was: 0 products successfully submitted to Google. There were 644 errors. All products returned the same error: To manage items via the API, the data source must have an API input type. API data sources cannot have a fileInput field set. It appears that the existing Merchant Center data source is configured as a file input, while the plugin is now attempting to manage products through the Merchant API. Could you please advise how to migrate or recreate the data source correctly without disconnecting the current Merchant Center and Google Ads accounts, and without creating duplicate products? https://pastebin.com/8qLzujqm shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi @sbentes ! Thank you for sharing the update and the detailed error message. The error suggests that your Merchant Center account is currently using a file-based data source , while the Google for WooCommerce plugin is attempting to submit products using the Merchant API . To assist you further, could you please first update the Google for WooCommerce plugin to the latest version 3.9.0 , and then try syncing your products again? If the issue persists after updating, please try disconnecting and reconnecting your Google accounts: From your WP Admin , go to Marketing → Google for WooCommerce → Settings . Click Disconnect from all accounts . Complete the setup again by reconnecting your Google account, Merchant Center account, and Google Ads account. Once the connection has been re-established, run Sync All Products with Google Merchant Center again. Reconnecting simply reauthorizes the connection and should not remove your Merchant Center or Google Ads accounts. If the issue still persists, could you please log in to your Google Merchant Center account, navigate to Products → Data sources , and share a screenshot of the Data sources page? That will help us verify how the data source is currently configured and determine why the plugin is unable to submit products through the Merchant API. Please let us know how it goes, and we’ll be happy to continue investigating with you. Thread Starter sbentes (@sbentes) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi! I updated Google for WooCommerce to version 3.9.0, disconnected all accounts, reconnected the Google, Merchant Center and Google Ads accounts, and tried “Sync All Products with Google Merchant Center” again. The issue persists. In Merchant Center → Settings → Data sources, I can see three primary sources: Merchant Center — Added in Merchant Center — 99 products Content API — 501 products — Needs update Google for WooCommerce (pt/PT) — File (URL) — 1,141 products I have attached a screenshot of the Data sources page. Could you please confirm which existing source should be retained or migrated before I remove or change anything? shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi @sbentes ! Thanks for sharing the details. I checked this with our team, and having three primary data sources can cause conflicts. Since you’re also using PixelYourSite , which may be syncing products to Google Merchant Center, I’d recommend the following: In Merchant Center → Settings → Data sources , remove other two sources. Keep the Google for WooCommerce (pt/PT) — File (URL) — 1,141 products source, as this is the source that can remain for the Merchant API integration. In WordPress, temporarily deactivate the PixelYourSite plugin so we can rule out another product feed/sync interfering with Google for WooCommerce. After that, go back to Google for WooCommerce and try “Sync All Products with Google Merchant Center” again. If the issue still occurs after this, please share the relevant error logs from the failed sync so we can investigate further. shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi @sbentes ! Just following up on my previous message with some additional information from our team regarding the Merchant Center data sources. If you don’t have any active Google Ads campaigns , our team recommends taking a clean approach to rule out any conflicting product feeds. Please first make sure that no other plugins are syncing products to Google Merchant Center. In particular, since you’re using PixelYourSite , please temporarily deactivate it, as it has an option to create and sync a product feed to GMC. If no other integrations are actively syncing products to GMC, you can then delete the existing data sources and set up Google for WooCommerce afresh. After the setup is complete, please try syncing your products to Google Merchant Center again. If the issue persists after the fresh setup, please share the relevant Google for WooCommerce logs with us so we can review them and investigate further. If you currently have active Google Ads campaigns using these product feeds, it would be best to wait until the campaign is completed , if it has a specific deadline. Alternatively, you can pause/stop the active ad campaigns before making changes to the Merchant Center data sources. Once the campaigns are no longer active, you can proceed with deleting the existing data sources and setting up Google for WooCommerce afresh as outlined in my previous message. After the new feed is set up and confirmed to be working correctly, you can enable your Google Ads campaigns again. This will help avoid disrupting any active campaigns while we clean up and recreate the product feeds. Please let us know how it goes, and we’ll be happy to continue investigating if the issue persists. Plugin Support Feten L. a11n (@fetenlakhal) 1 month, 4 weeks ago Hi there, As we haven’t received a response in some time, I’ll mark this ticket as resolved. Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you need further assistance. Viewing 11 replies - 1 through 11 (of 11 total) You must be logged in to reply to this topic. title: Google for WooCommerce 3.9.5 – Merchant API data source error and recurring sche | WordPress.org
text: Google for WooCommerce 3.9.5 – Merchant API data source error and recurring sche | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / Google for WooCommerce 3.9.5 – Merchant API data source error and recurring sche Search for: Search forums Google for WooCommerce 3.9.5 – Merchant API data source error and recurring sche sbentes (@sbentes) 6 days, 17 hours ago Hello, We are experiencing recurring synchronization errors with Google for WooCommerce 3.9.5. Our store is connected to Google Merchant Center, but the plugin is generating errors when updating products through the Merchant API and retrieving product statuses. Issue 1 – Merchant API data source error The WooCommerce logs repeatedly show: [dataSource] To manage items via the API, the data source must have an API input type. API data sources cannot have a fileInput field set. Product updates fail with 0 succeeded, 1 failed . Issue 2 – Scheduled action failures The scheduled action gla/jobs/update_merchant_product_statuses/process_item repeatedly fails with: MerchantStatuses::parse_presync_issue_text(): Argument #1 ($text) must be of type string, array given Eventually, the scheduled job is paused because its failure rate exceeds the allowed threshold. Merchant Center configuration Our Merchant Center account has two relevant primary product data sources: Content API: 315 products, API type, Source ID 10584122856. The most recently updated products we found date from July 2026. Google for WooCommerce (pt/PT): 1,141 active products, File (URL) type. This XML feed is generated by a separate plugin, Woo Product Feed Pro, and is successfully updated daily. Both sources use Portugal as the target country and Portuguese as the language. Additional information Google for WooCommerce version: 3.9.5 Store platform: WooCommerce / WordPress Merchant Center connection: Connected Google Ads connection: Connected Scheduled actions run through WP-Cron Could you please advise: Why the plugin appears to be attempting API product updates using a file-based data source? How we can correct the data source association without deleting existing products or affecting the functioning XML feed? Whether a fix is available for the parse_presync_issue_text() type error? How to safely resume the paused scheduled job after correcting the underlying issue? We want to preserve the existing Merchant Center products, the functioning XML feed, and our Google Ads conversion tracking. Thank you. Viewing 4 replies - 1 through 4 (of 4 total) Plugin Support Jason Kytros (@jasonkytros) 5 days, 18 hours ago Hey @sbentes , This is Jason, a Technical Product Manager working on Google for WooCommerce. Thank you for your report! Both issues are currently being worked on: Our team is currently reviewing a fix for feeds being incorrectly classified as a file input data source. The “Argument #1 ($text) must be of type string, array given” error was previously reported here , so I prioritized working on a fix , given that this is the second report we got about this issue. When the fixes move to the “Merged” status, then this means that they will be included in the next release. I will keep you posted on our progress! Aniket Patel (@aniketpatel) 5 days, 2 hours ago Hi Jason Kytros , We’re experiencing the same issue after updating the plugin to version 3.9.5, and approximately 500 products are affected. Could you please investigate and resolve this issue as soon as possible? It’s impacting our sales, so we would appreciate your urgent assistance. Thank you Thread Starter sbentes (@sbentes) 4 days, 18 hours ago Hi Jason, Thank you for your quick response and for prioritizing these issues. I’m glad to hear that both fixes are being worked on. I’ll keep the current configuration unchanged and wait for the fixes to be included in an official release. Please keep me updated when the fixes are available. Thanks again for your help! Plugin Support Saravanan S, a11n (@simplysaru) 3 days, 22 hours ago Hey there @aniketpatel and @sbentes , Thanks for your patience & understanding so far, and currently the bug fix is in QA and we expect it to be merged soon. We will follow up once the fix is released. Viewing 4 replies - 1 through 4 (of 4 total) You must be logged in to reply to this topic. title: Google for WooCommerce 3.9.6 stuck loading and sync fails | WordPress.org
text: Google for WooCommerce 3.9.6 stuck loading and sync fails | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / Google for WooCommerce 3.9.6 stuck loading and sync fails Search for: Search forums Google for WooCommerce 3.9.6 stuck loading and sync fails 7leguas (@7leguas) 3 days, 17 hours ago Hello, I need help troubleshooting Google for WooCommerce on my store: https://7leguas.mx/ . Environment: Google for WooCommerce / Google Listings & Ads: version 3.9.6 WooCommerce: version 11.0.1 PHP: 8.1.34 Server: LiteSpeed WordPress memory limit reported in the error log: 384 MB Issue: Google for WooCommerce’s Overview page keeps loading indefinitely, and no products are appearing in Google Merchant Center. Merchant Center says that no products have been added. The product feed setup page says that the setup is complete and there are no issues to resolve, but the Overview page never finishes loading. I also tried opening the plugin’s troubleshooting tool, but WooCommerce and Google for WooCommerce appeared as inactive in troubleshooting mode, and WordPress said that the required dependency was missing. Relevant fatal error from the WordPress log: Allowed memory size of 402653184 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 20480 bytes) The error occurred in /wp-includes/class-wpdb.php , line 2328. I checked WooCommerce Scheduled Actions and found some pending Google for WooCommerce actions, but no recent failed Google Listings & Ads actions. Could you help me determine whether this is a memory/database query issue, a plugin conflict, or a bug in version 3.9.6? I would like to get product synchronization working without disconnecting my existing Google Merchant Center account or losing its configuration. Thank you. The page I need help with: [ log in to see the link] Viewing 3 replies - 1 through 3 (of 3 total) Plugin Support Saravanan S, a11n (@simplysaru) 2 days, 22 hours ago Hi @7leguas , Thanks for the detailed report — the environment info and the fatal error from your log are really helpful. Google for WooCommerce syncs products in the background using Action Scheduler (it submits products to Google via the Merchant API as queued batch jobs). A few of your symptoms line up with that background queue not completing rather than a settings problem: the Overview page hanging, no products reaching Merchant Center, pending Google jobs in Scheduled Actions, and the Allowed memory size … exhausted fatal in class-wpdb.php . If the queue can’t finish (because a job hits the memory limit, or because WP-Cron/loopback requests aren’t firing), products never get submitted even though the feed setup page reports “complete.” So before we go further, could you check whether Action Scheduler is actually processing at all: Go to WooCommerce → Status → Scheduled Actions , filter by Pending , and look at the date on the oldest pending action. If the oldest pending job is more than a day or two old and keeps growing, the queue is backed up / not running — usually a WP-Cron or server loopback issue, and worth asking your host to confirm WP-Cron and loopback requests are allowed and that long-running background processes aren’t being killed. If pending jobs ARE clearing but products still don’t appear in Merchant Center, that points more at the plugin/API connection and we’d dig into the logs instead. Could you tell me the date of the oldest Pending action in that list, and whether the pending count is going down over time or staying stuck or increasing consistently? A couple of other things that will help us narrow it down: Please grab your System Status Report (WooCommerce → Status → Get system report → Copy for support) and paste it to https://pastebin.com/ and share the link. It’ll show us your real PHP memory limit and WP-Cron status. Check WooCommerce → Status → Logs and open the most recent google-for-woocommerce log — if there are errors there, paste the relevant lines. Also, if there are any recent fatal error logs, please do share them as well. Please feel free to remove any confidential details from the logs. The troubleshooting-mode behaviour you saw (WooCommerce and Google for WooCommerce showing as inactive) is expected — Troubleshooting Mode temporarily disables all plugins except the one being tested, which is why dependencies looked missing; that on its own isn’t a sign of a problem. None of this requires disconnecting your Merchant Center account, so you won’t lose your configuration while we look into it. We look forward to hearing back from you as soon as possible. Thread Starter 7leguas (@7leguas) 2 days, 17 hours ago Hello Saravanan, Thank you for your guidance. I completed the requested checks for my WooCommerce store, https://7leguas.mx/ , and found several issues that may be related to the Google for WooCommerce synchronization problem. 1. Action Scheduler status I checked WooCommerce → Status → Scheduled Actions and found the following: Pending actions: 7,902. Oldest pending action: February 24, 2026, at 17:30:40 UTC-6. Queue progress: I waited ten minutes and refreshed the list, but the pending count did not decrease. Migration warning: WooCommerce displays “Action Scheduler migration in progress. The list of scheduled actions may be incomplete.” Failed actions: 4,714. In-progress actions: 1. The System Status Report also shows that the wp_actionscheduler_actions table uses approximately 492 MB, including indexes, and the wp_actionscheduler_logs table uses approximately 240 MB, including indexes. Could this indicate that Action Scheduler is stalled or that its migration has not completed successfully? 2. Google for WooCommerce logs I reviewed the logs for October 13 and October 14, 2026. Log: google-for-woocommerce-2026-10-13 I found the following entries: cURL error 28: AccountService::is_wpcom_api_status_healthy timed out after approximately 30 seconds with zero bytes received. Google Ads incentive error: ACCOUNT_TOO_OLD . Google rejected an advertising incentive because too much time had passed since the account’s first ad impression. WordPress.com token revocation error: No token found associated with the client ID and user . The debug entries also show the plugin mapping WooCommerce product categories, including Continental, Yokohama, Kumho, and Pirelli. However, I cannot confirm that the products were successfully synchronized to Merchant Center. Log: google-for-woocommerce-2026-10-14 I found the same ACCOUNT_TOO_OLD error when the plugin attempted to apply the Google Ads incentive. I understand that the incentive error may be unrelated to product synchronization. However, could the cURL timeout or token-related error indicate a problem with the current connection or the plugin’s ability to communicate with its services? 3. WooCommerce System Status Report The report shows the following environment details: WordPress: 6.9.1. WooCommerce: 11.0.1. Google for WooCommerce: 3.9.6. Action Scheduler: 4.1.0. PHP: 8.1.34. WordPress memory limit: 384 MB. Server: LiteSpeed. Database size: approximately 1.75 GB. Products in WooCommerce: 3,817. Remote POST and GET requests are available. The WP-Cron status appears as a dash in the report, so I cannot confirm whether scheduled tasks are running correctly. Previously, I also encountered this WordPress fatal error: Allowed memory size of 402653184 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 20480 bytes) The error occurred in wp-includes/class-wpdb.php , line 2328. System Status Report: https://pastebin.com/JLp2h7JX Current symptoms The Google for WooCommerce Overview page spins indefinitely. No products appear in Google Merchant Center. Action Scheduler has thousands of pending actions, and the queue did not advance during my five-minute check. A memory exhaustion error has occurred previously. Questions Could you please advise on the safest next steps to: Verify whether WP-Cron, loopback requests, and background processing are working correctly. Diagnose and safely complete the Action Scheduler migration, if it is stuck. Determine whether the cURL timeout or WordPress.com token error affects Google for WooCommerce. Restore product synchronization with Merchant Center without risking existing products, orders, or other store data. I have not manually run or deleted the pending actions, and I have not revoked or reset any tokens. Thank you for your help. Plugin Support Saravanan S, a11n (@simplysaru) 2 days ago Hi @7leguas , Thank you for the thorough response — these details make the root cause clear. Your Action Scheduler queue is completely stalled. Seven thousand nine hundred twelve pending actions, oldest dating back to February, plus a migration that never completed, means the background processing system your store uses for scheduled tasks has effectively frozen. Google for WooCommerce relies on Action Scheduler to run sync jobs, so when the queue doesn’t process, products never reach Merchant Center. The huge tables (wp_actionscheduler_actions at ~492 MB and wp_actionscheduler_logs at ~240 MB) are the direct result of thousands of failed jobs accumulating over months. The memory exhaustion error you saw in class-wpdb.php was likely caused by WordPress trying to read or query these oversized tables. The cURL timeout on the WordPress.com API health check is a symptom of the overall system strain, not the root cause. The ACCOUNT_TOO_OLD error is unrelated to sync — it just means a Google Ads incentive expired, and needs to fixed. The WordPress.com token error is also a downstream effect of the Action Scheduler being unable to complete the token-refresh jobs it had queued. Here’s what I recommend doing next, in order: Clear the failed actions — Go to WooCommerce → Status → Scheduled Actions, switch to the “Failed” tab, and delete all 4,714 failed actions. This is safe and won’t affect your products, orders, or Google connection. You can do this by clicking “Delete all failed” if that option appears, or by deleting them in batches. Run the Action Scheduler migration manually — After clearing failed actions, try the migration again. If it gets stuck, you can force-complete it by adding this to wp-config.php temporarily: define(‘action_scheduler_queue_lock_timeouts’, 0); Then visit the action scheduler migration page or trigger wp cron. Remove the line afterward. Verify the queue is moving — After the migration completes, refresh the Scheduled Actions page and confirm pending actions are being processed (the count should start decreasing). Resetup Google for WooCommerce sync — Once Action Scheduler is running normally, go to the Google for WooCommerce settings page and disconnect all accounts. This should disconnect the plugin and help you start afresh with the setup. Please ensure you have a Google ads account setup and configured correctly with a payment method even if you want to configure free listings only. once the setup completes, product sync will be triggered automatically. Monitor for new memory issues — With 3,817 products, 384 MB PHP memory is workable but tight. If you see memory errors again, consider increasing it to 512 MB, especially during sync operations. The Overview page hangs because Google for WooCommerce tries to load data while the Action Scheduler migration is in progress. Once the migration completes, the Overview should load normally. Please let me know how the clearing of failed actions and the migration go, and whether the queue starts processing afterwards. text: JS Type Error: Cannto Read Properties of Undefined (email) | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / JS Type Error: Cannto Read Properties of Undefined (email) Search for: Search forums JS Type Error: Cannto Read Properties of Undefined (email) Resolved Jim (@jimrgbssmg) 2 months, 1 week ago I am getting a JS error message on the admin settings page: Oops, something went wrong We’re sorry for the inconvenience. Please try reloading the page, or you can get support from the community forums. react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:121 TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading ’email’) at y (commons.js?ver=87b47d498113d2918336:85:5280) at mf (react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:105:412) at Qk (react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:250:214) at Ri (react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:195:185) at Ok (react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:195:116) at Nd (react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:194:492) at Qf (react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:187:439) at Li (react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:189:234) at db (react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:79:182) at react-dom.min.js?ver=18.3.1.1:184:289 Viewing 5 replies - 1 through 5 (of 5 total) shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi @jimrgbssmg ! I can see you are running into a JavaScript error on the Google for WooCommerce settings page, where it is trying to read the email property from an undefined value. That definitely points to something not loading correctly in the setup or a conflict interfering with the data being passed. To help narrow this down, could you please confirm the following: Are you able to complete the Google account connection flow, or does the error appear before or during setup Have you recently updated WooCommerce or the Google for WooCommerce plugin before this started happening In the meantime, please try the steps below as they often help isolate this type of issue: Clear your browser cache and try again in an incognito window Temporarily deactivate all plugins except WooCommerce and Google for WooCommerce, then test again Switch to a default theme like Storefront and check if the issue persists You can follow this guide for running a full conflict test: https://woocommerce.com/document/how-to-test-for-conflicts/ If you still face the same issue even after running a conflict test, could you please share the System Status Report from WooCommerce → Status and any relevant error logs from WooCommerce → Status → Logs ? Please paste both in Pastebin and share the generated Pastebin links with us. When creating the Pastebin entries, please enable the Burn after reading option. This will allow us to review the information and investigate the issue further. Thread Starter Jim (@jimrgbssmg) 2 months ago Hi shahzeen, I did all of that. When I just use incognito mode in the browser I am able to see all the pages except settings. However the “Google Ads” section on the dashboard fails to load and these two errors appear in the console: GET /wp-json/wc/gla/ads/settings?_locale=user 403 (Forbidden) index.js?ver=6d3d441a3c6aa2c9ac3e:1 Not Allowed. It shows the free feed as enabled. The report tab works fine and shows the product feed, clicks, impressions, etc. the Product feed tab will load with the product feed and a few issues (availability date for backorder/preorder), but the overview section (active, expiring, pending, disapproved, not synced) spins and spins and never loads. However, is says the product feed setup is completed. The price benchmark, attributes, and markets tabs all load fine. The settings page will partially load. I see it with a “Linked Accounts” section with a loading icon for a second or two then the Cannot read properties of undefined (reading ’email’) error happens. The same thing listed above happens on a staging site with all other plugins disabled. If you can provide a private message or email I can send the pastebin. Plugin Support Feten L. a11n (@fetenlakhal) 2 months ago Hi @jimrgbssmg , Thank you for running through all of that and for the detailed follow-up. The Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'email') error looks like a symptom rather than the root cause here. A few things that would help me narrow this down: Connection owner : Is the admin account you’re logged in as the same one that originally connected the site to WordPress.com/Jetpack? You can check under Jetpack → My Jetpack → Connection . If the connection is owned by a different user, the GLA endpoints can return Not Allowed. for everyone else. Google Ads link : Under Marketing → Google for WooCommerce , is a Google Ads account actually linked, or is only Merchant Center connected? Server-level filtering : Because staging behaves identically with plugins off, it’s worth ruling out something above WordPress. Could you check with your host whether ModSecurity, a WAF, or any REST API restriction is active? Logs : Please grab WooCommerce → Status → Logs and check for entries with the source google-listings-and-ads . On the Pastebin: you can post the Pastebin links here directly, and if you enable the Burn after reading option when creating them, the content is destroyed as soon as I open it. Looking forward to your reply. Thread Starter Jim (@jimrgbssmg) 2 months ago I don’t have Jetpack installed so not sure what account is connected, that portion was set up years ago by someone else – does it require Jetpack? Only Merchant Center is connected They are using Cloudflare WAF but not on the server itself Please provide a DM for that. Anyone can open it and see it and would burn prior to you opening the link. shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 1 month, 4 weeks ago Hi @jimrgbssmg ! Thanks for sharing those additional details. That helps clarify the setup. Jetpack itself is not required for the Google for WooCommerce integration. Since only Merchant Center is connected, the issue may be related to the existing Google account connection or its permissions. For more details you can read this guide: https://woocommerce.com/document/google-for-woocommerce/faq/ Before troubleshooting further, I’d recommend checking the Google Ads account first and then testing the issue again. Alternatively, I suggest reconnecting the Google account and Merchant Center connection by following these steps: Go to https://example.com/wp-admin/admin.php?page=connection-test-admin-page Under Merchant Center , click MC Disconnect . Under Google Account , click Disconnect Google Account . In your Google Account’s security settings, remove the existing access permissions for WooCommerce. Return to the plugin and repeat the setup process. You can also follow our guide for the complete setup process: Google for W ooCommerce – Setup and Configuration Regarding the System Status Report, unfortunately, we don’t have a separate DM option for sharing it. I understand your concern about the report being publicly accessible. You can set a short expiration time when sharing it, or use Pastebin’s Burn After Read option. In most cases, we can access the report before anyone else opens it. Since you’re also using Cloudflare WAF, it would be useful to temporarily disable the WAF and test the issue again. This will help us determine whether Cloudflare is interfering with the connection. Once you’ve tried these steps, please let us know what you find. The results will help us narrow down the cause and determine the next steps. Viewing 5 replies - 1 through 5 (of 5 total) You must be logged in to reply to this topic. title: Migrating to the new Merchant API | WordPress.org
text: Migrating to the new Merchant API | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / Migrating to the new Merchant API Search for: Search forums Migrating to the new Merchant API Resolved Tishina (@gkaralov) 4 months, 2 weeks ago Hello, I got an email from Google quoting: Migrate to Merchant API before August 18, 2026 To simplify how you manage your business and how your products show up on Google, the new Merchant API is replacing the Content API* for Shopping. You’ll get a more reliable way to update product information automatically, along with easy access to insights and new capabilities like real-time notifications. Will this plugin handle the migration to the new Merchant API or it’s something I should do manually myself? Thanks in advance for the answer! Viewing 9 replies - 1 through 9 (of 9 total) Frank Remmy (@frankremmy) 4 months, 2 weeks ago Hi @gkaralov , Thanks for reaching out about the Google Merchant API migration notice. Will this plugin handle the migration to the new Merchant API or it’s something I should do manually myself? No manual action needed on your end. The migration from the Content API for Shopping to the new Google Merchant API is being actively handled within the Google for WooCommerce plugin, and the transition is expected to happen automatically through upcoming plugin updates. The main thing you should do is make sure the plugin stays updated. Keeping it on the latest version ensures you’ll receive the Merchant API migration as it rolls out, well before the August 18, 2026 deadline. You can also verify your current status in Google Merchant Center: go to Settings → Data Sources and check the Source column. If it already shows “Merchant API” you’re good. If it still shows “Content API”, the plugin update will handle the switch. Hope that puts your mind at ease. Let us know if anything else comes up! Thread Starter Tishina (@gkaralov) 4 months, 2 weeks ago Thank you for the answer! 🙂 shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 4 months, 2 weeks ago Hi there! You are welcome. Before you go, If you found Google for WooCommerce helpful in setting up your store, we would really appreciate it if you could leave a five-star review here: https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/google-listings-and-ads/reviews/#new-post . Your feedback helps us improve and lets other users know how Google for WooCommerce can support their business. weseo (@weseo) 3 months, 3 weeks ago Hi @frankremmy , how can I prove that the migration worked. After the update I checked the status in Google Merchant Center and now I see “Merchant API” and “Content API”, but the row of “Merchant Center” still shows 0 products. I checked it a few days later and still 0 products synced. In my opinion it still syncs to the old “Content API”. Thanks in advance for the answer! shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 3 months, 3 weeks ago Hi @weseo ! To keep the discussion organized and ensure your issue receives the attention it deserves, could you please create a new support topic for your issue instead of posting it in this thread? This thread is related to another user’s issue, and creating a separate topic helps us track and troubleshoot each case more effectively. Also, as per forum best practices shown here , it is advised that you create a new thread so that we can address your issue(s) separately. You can create a new thread here: https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/woocommerce/#new-topic-0 and make sure to include as much information as you can. Thank you for cooperation and understanding. Thread Starter Tishina (@gkaralov) 2 months, 1 week ago Hello again, I updated the plugin to the newest version two days ago since Merchant API should be available now but in my GMC the data source still shows up as Content API? Is this normal? https://prnt.sc/scJIcixxJZpL Plugin Support Saravanan S, a11n (@simplysaru) 2 months, 1 week ago Hi @gkaralov , Thanks for the follow up. Yes, it is normal to see the source in the GMC dashboard as Content API. Your data source might continue to show Content API in Google Merchant Center for existing merchants even after using version 3.8.1 or later; this means the source details haven’t been updated in the dashboard, but the underlying API has been updated. The plugin syncs to the same source ID using the new Merchant center API endpoint. You can verify this in the debug logs with the product synced via the MAPI endpoint denoted by WooCommerce\GoogleListingsAndAds\API\Google\Mapi\MerchantApiClient: . Also, the feed would now show a language attribute next to Google for WooCommerce. In your case it’s the RO for Romanian. https://cleanshot.com/share/LfxCBD81 which is specific to the merchant API. Thread Starter Tishina (@gkaralov) 2 months ago Great. Thank you so much! 🙂 shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months ago Hi @gkaralov ! You’re very welcome! It was a pleasure helping you. If you need any further assistance in the future, please feel free to create a new support ticket. We’ll be happy to help! title: Product sync issue – Most products rejected due to availability date error | WordPress.org
text: Product sync issue – Most products rejected due to availability date error | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / Product sync issue – Most products rejected due to availability date error Search for: Search forums Product sync issue – Most products rejected due to availability date error Resolved robin6990 (@robin6990) 4 months ago Hello, I am experiencing an issue with the Google for WooCommerce (Google Listings & Ads) plugin. The plugin successfully generated and submitted the product feed, but only 16 products were imported into Google Merchant Center. All the remaining products were rejected due to an error related to the availability date . What I find confusing is that the availability information is already defined for all products according to their stock status in WooCommerce. Because of this, I don’t understand why Merchant Center is reporting an availability date error for most products. Could you please clarify: How does the plugin generate the availability_date attribute? Under what conditions is this error triggered? Is there a known issue where stock status and availability date are not synchronized correctly? Is there any log or diagnostic tool I can use to identify which product data is causing the problem? At the moment: Feed generation completes successfully. 16 products are accepted. All other products are rejected because of the availability date attribute. Any guidance would be greatly appreciated. Thank you. Viewing 2 replies - 1 through 2 (of 2 total) Frank Remmy (@frankremmy) 3 months, 4 weeks ago Hi @robin6990 , Great questions! Good news, this has a real, supported fix without needing custom code. Here’s the mechanism: Google requires an availability_date for any product marked backorder or preorder , this applies to both, not just preorder. Your products with WooCommerce stock status “On backorder” are getting flagged because that date isn’t set yet. The 16 accepted products are likely your in-stock or out-of-stock items, since only backorder/preorder require this field. To fix it: open any affected product’s edit screen, look for the “Google for WooCommerce” tab alongside the usual Inventory/Shipping tabs, you’ll find an “Availability Date” field there to set manually. To see exactly which products are affected and why, go to Marketing → Google for WooCommerce → Product Feed, which lists per-product sync status and the specific issue for each one. By any chance, how many products were affected? If your store has a consistent restock timeframe, you could streamline this with a small code snippet using the woocommerce_gla_product_attribute_values filter to set a calculated date automatically for all backordered products, that kind of custom development is outside our direct support scope , but WooExperts or Codeable could help build that for you if you’d like it automated. I hope that helps. Let us know if you need anything else. Plugin Support Kay U a11n (@kingsleyinfo) 3 months, 2 weeks ago It seems we haven’t heard back from you for a while, so I’ll go ahead and mark this thread as resolved. Feel free to reach out whenever you’re ready to continue. Viewing 2 replies - 1 through 2 (of 2 total) You must be logged in to reply to this topic. title: Product sync silently fails | WordPress.org
text: Product sync silently fails | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / Product sync silently fails Search for: Search forums Product sync silently fails Resolved brice08 (@brice08) 2 months ago Hi, Product sync stopped on my store around 20 July 2026 and I cannot restore it. Products are now expiring out of Merchant Center (499 → 470 in a few hours) and I have lost most of my free listings traffic. Environment Google for WooCommerce: 3.9.0 (updated from 3.8.1 today, the issue predates the update) WordPress 7.0.4, WooCommerce current, PHP 8.x, host: WPServeur Merchant Center account: 114246480 (ritesbijoux.com) Products: 133 WooCommerce products (~499 variations) Symptoms All products report not_synced . GET /wc/gla/mc/product-feed returns status: not_synced for 133/133 products. GET /wc/gla/mc/connection returns: { "id": 114246480, "status": "connected", "wpcom_rest_api_status": "error" } Everything else reports healthy: GET /wc/gla/mc/setup → {"status":"complete"} GET /wc/gla/mc/review → {"status":"APPROVED","issues":[]} GET /wc/gla/jetpack/connected → {"active":"yes","owner":"yes"} GET /wc/gla/google/connected → active, scopes include .../auth/content GET /wc/gla/google/reconnected → merchant_access: "yes" , merchant_account: 114246480 POST /wc/gla/mc/settings/sync → "Successfully synchronized settings with Google." A full resync ( update_all_products , triggered via POST /wc/gla/mc/settings/sync ) schedules and completes its Action Scheduler jobs — create_batch and process_item actions complete with real product IDs — but no product is ever marked as synced. gla/jobs/update_merchant_product_statuses/process_item fails repeatedly and gets paused (“failure rate above the allowed threshold”). Before updating to 3.9.0, GET /wc/gla/mc/product-statistics returned a fatal error: MerchantStatuses::parse_presync_issue_text(): Argument #1 ($text) must be of type string, array given,called in .../src/MerchantCenter/MerchantStatuses.php on line 697 That specific fatal is gone in 3.9.0, but the job still fails. Merchant Center → Data sources still shows only the legacy Content API source (470 products, “Update needed”, last update empty). No Merchant API data source was ever created, even though 3.8.0 migrated to the Merchant API. The blocking problem Since wpcom_rest_api_status is error , the extension should let me grant access again. But the re-authorization URL is itself invalid: GET /wc/gla/rest-api/authorize?next_page_name=settings returns an auth_url pointing to https://public-api.wordpress.com/oauth2/authorize containing only blog , response_type , scope=wc-partner-access and state — client_id and redirect_uri are missing , and the state payload contains only store_url , without the expected nonce . Loading that URL returns: Error Code: invalid_requestError Message: The required "redirect_uri" parameter is missing. Reading OAuthService::get_auth_url() , those three values come from get_data_from_google() → Middleware::get_sdi_auth_params() , which appears to return empty. That call goes through the same WPCOM connection that is reported as broken — so the documented recovery path depends on the very connection it is meant to repair. I cannot re-grant access from the extension UI. What I already tried (no change) Updated the extension from 3.8.1 to 3.9.0. This removed the parse_presync_issue_text() fatal, but product sync still does not work. Triggered a full resync several times via POST /wc/gla/mc/settings/sync . Action Scheduler shows gla/jobs/update_all_products/create_batch and process_item actions completing successfully with no errors logged , yet no product is ever marked as synced. After the last run, product status went from not_synced to null for all 133 products — the records are reset but never populated. Reconnected the Jetpack / WordPress.com site connection (via the connect URL returned by GET /wc/gla/jetpack/connect , authorized on jetpack.wordpress.com). No change : wpcom_rest_api_status is still error and products still do not sync. Note: AccountService::get_connected_status() only re-evaluates health when the stored status is approved ( if ( $wpcom_rest_api_status === 'approved' && ! $this->is_wpcom_api_status_healthy() ) ). Once it has been set to error it is never re-tested or reset, so I cannot tell from that field whether the underlying connection recovered. That looks like a bug in its own right. gla/jobs/resubmit_expiring_products runs daily but is a no-op here: find_expiring_product_ids() requires the _wc_gla_synced_at meta, which no product has, so create_batch completes with cursor 0 and never creates any process_item . This means there is no automatic recovery path once sync state is lost. Questions How can I re-establish the WPCOM ↔ Google partner authorization when get_sdi_auth_params() returns empty? Will reconnecting Jetpack / refreshing my personal WPCOM user token fix this, and will it put my remaining products at risk? Is there a supported way to force creation of the Merchant API data source without disconnecting the Merchant Center account (I do not want to lose the products still serving)? I would rather not disconnect the Merchant Center account, as the remaining products are still generating free-listing traffic. Thanks, Brice — ritesbijoux.com Viewing 2 replies - 1 through 2 (of 2 total) Thread Starter brice08 (@brice08) 2 months ago The root cause was on the Merchant Center side, not in the connection. My account had 4 data sources, all with contentLanguage fr and feedLabel FR . Two of them were old, paused Google Sheets feeds with 0 products (“Google for WooCommerce (fr/FR)” and one other). MapiDataSourcesService::find_existing_data_source() returns the FIRST data source matching contentLanguage + feedLabel, without checking that the source accepts API writes. So the plugin resolved its data source to a spreadsheet feed, and Google rejected every product with: [dataSource] To manage items via the API, the data source must have an API input type. API data sources cannot have a fileInput field set. Action Scheduler jobs (update_all_products, resubmit_expiring_products) completed normally and swallowed this error, so nothing surfaced anywhere in the UI. The only way I found it was the hidden Connection Test page → Product Sync → “Sync Product” with Async unchecked, which runs synchronously and prints the raw errors. Fix: I deleted the two Google Sheets data sources in Merchant Center. The plugin then adopted the legacy “Content API” source and renamed it “Google for WooCommerce (fr/FR)”, products stayed in place, and sync resumed immediately. Suggestion for the developers: find_existing_data_source() should skip data sources that have a fileInput field, and the product syncer should surface dataSource errors instead of letting the batch job complete silently. This reply was modified 2 months ago by Jan Dembowski . Reason: Formattng shahzeen(woo-hc) (@shahzeenfarooq) 2 months ago Hi @brice08 ! Thank you for the detailed investigation and for sharing the root cause and fix. It’s very helpful to know that the issue was caused by the Merchant Center selecting an old Google Sheets data source instead of an API-compatible data source. I’m also glad to hear that deleting the two old data sources allowed the plugin to adopt the correct source and that product syncing resumed immediately. Your suggestions regarding skipping data sources with a fileInput field and surfacing the dataSource errors from Action Scheduler are also very useful. I’ll make sure this feedback is shared with the developers for consideration. Thanks again for taking the time to investigate this so thoroughly. This information should be very helpful to other users who may encounter the same issue. Viewing 2 replies - 1 through 2 (of 2 total) You must be logged in to reply to this topic. text: v8.0.1 BestPrice template outputs Y/N availability, products rejected | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Product Feed Manager for WooCommerce – CTX Feed – Support 220+ Shopping, AI & Social Channels / v8.0.1 BestPrice template outputs Y/N availability, products rejected Search for: Search forums v8.0.1 BestPrice template outputs Y/N availability, products rejected Resolved Miltiadis (@zafeiropoulos) 1 month, 2 weeks ago Since updating CTX Feed from 6.6.23 to 8.0.1, the BestPrice.gr XML template converts the availability value to Y/N. BestPrice.gr does not accept those values, so my entire catalogue is now rejected. Steps to reproduce: Create an XML feed using the BestPrice.gr template. Map the availability attribute to the product stock status. Generate the feed and inspect the availability node. Output on 6.6.23 (accepted by BestPrice): 1-3 ημέρες Output on 8.0.1 (rejected): N The value is converted to Y/N regardless of what the source attribute contains. The BestPrice.gr merchant panel flags all products as faulty with the error “Μη διαθέσιμη πληροφορία διαθεσιμότητας στο αρχείο XML” (no availability information in the XML file). The Yes/No format mentioned on your feature page is outdated. The current BestPrice.gr specification requires one of these exact strings: Σε απόθεμα Παράδοση σε 1-3 ημέρες Παράδοση σε 4-7 ημέρες Παράδοση σε 4-10 ημέρες Παράδοση σε 8-14 ημέρες Παράδοση σε 15-30 ημέρες Κατόπιν παραγγελίας Προπαραγγελία Εξαντλήθηκε Could you either update the BestPrice.gr template to output these values, or add a way to bypass the conversion so the source attribute is passed through unchanged? A static value is not an option because availability varies per product, and Dynamic Attributes are Pro-only. I have rolled back to 6.6.23 for now, which works correctly. Environment: WordPress 7.1 WooCommerce 11.0.1 PHP 8.5.9 (64-bit) CTX Feed (free) 8.0.1 — broken CTX Feed (free) 6.6.23 — works Feed format: XML, BestPrice.gr template Viewing 1 replies (of 1 total) Plugin Support mansary (@mansary) 1 month, 2 weeks ago Hi @zafeiropoulos Thanks for your time and patience. We have recently released a new version of CTX Feed, version 8.0.9 , which includes updates and fixes. Could you please update CTX Feed to the latest version and check whether this resolves the issue on your website? After updating, please let us know whether the latest version has resolved the problem. We appreciate your patience and cooperation. Februar 2026 um 11:26 HL Berlin aktiv. Mitglied Punkte 10 Beiträge 1 19. Februar 2026 um 11:26 #1 Hi, I'm having issues with Google for WooCommerce not syncing products to Google Merchant Center, despite everything appearing to be working correctly. SETUP: - Site: hardmann.eu - Merchant Center ID: 571792XXX - Merchant Center domain: hardmann.eu (claimed and verified) - Google Ads ID: 9106125XXX - Plugin version: [Latest from wordpress.org] - WooCommerce version: [Check: WooCommerce → Status] - WordPress version: [Check: Dashboard → Updates] ISSUE: ✅ Plugin shows "Connected" status ✅ API endpoint /wp-json/wc/gla/mc/connection returns {"status":"connected","id":571792XXX} ✅ Product feed shows 21 products ✅ Action Scheduler shows all 21 actions as "complete" ❌ All products remain in "not_synced" status ❌ Products are NOT appearing in Google Merchant Center STEPS ALREADY TAKEN: 1. Completely reinstalled the plugin 2. Reconnected all Google accounts (Google Account, Merchant Center, Google Ads) 3. Cleared all WordPress caches and transients 4. Manually triggered Action Scheduler (all 21 actions completed successfully) 5. Verified no issues via /wp-json/wc/gla/mc/issues (returns {"issues":[],"total":0}) 6. Set up WP-Cron to run every 15 minutes via Plesk scheduled task 7. Manually executed do_action('woocommerce_gla_update_product', $product_id) for all 21 products 8. Verified all products are published, have price > 0, and are in stock 9. Set setup completion flags in database manually API RESPONSES: - /wp-json/wc/gla/mc/product-feed → 21 products, all with status: "not_synced" - /wp-json/wc/gla/mc/connection → {"status":"connected","id":571792XXX} - /wp-json/wc/gla/mc/issues → {"issues":[],"total":0} - Action Scheduler database: All 21 actions show status: "complete" OBSERVATION: The plugin executes all Action Scheduler jobs successfully, but the actual push to Google Content API never happens. Products remain in "not_synced" state indefinitely. QUESTION: Is there a way to: 1. Manually force the Content API sync? 2. Debug why the API push is failing despite successful action completion? 3. Enable debug logging for Google Content API requests? ADDITIONAL CONTEXT: - I can provide full System Report if needed - The connection to Google is working (REST API confirms "connected") - Issue persists with all caches disabled - No errors in PHP error log or WordPress debug.log Wordpress 6.9.1 WooCommerce 10.5.2 Google for WooCoommerce 3.5.2 Any help would be greatly appreciated! This has been going on for several hours and I've exhausted all troubleshooting options. Thank you! Inhalt melden Zitieren Online Werbepost Bot Gerade eben Anzeige Hallo! Wenn du gerade an deiner Website arbeitest oder dein aktuelles Hosting überdenkst: Wir betreiben mit NetzLiving eine Hosting-Plattform, die speziell auf Performance, Sicherheit und einfache Verwaltung ausgelegt ist. ✔️ Schnelle Ladezeiten (optimiert für WordPress & Co.) ✔️ Deutsche Server & DSGVO-konform ✔️ Persönlicher Support (kein 0815-Ticket-System) Mehr erfahren Zu netzliving.eu wppoland aktiv. Mitglied Punkte 20 Beiträge 4 30. Juli 2026 um 14:12 #2 The one endpoint you have not checked is the one that would explain this. /mc/connection reports the Merchant Center link, not a successful product push, so it stays connected even when every upload is rejected. The pushes go out through the WooCommerce Connect proxy, and when they fail there the Action Scheduler job still completes, which is exactly the mismatch you are seeing: actions complete, products stay not_synced, and the issues endpoint has nothing because nothing ever reached the Content API. The logs will tell you in a minute. The plugin already logs by default (the woocommerce_gla_enable_debug_logging filter is on unless something turned it off), and the entries land in WooCommerce > Status > Logs under the source google-for-woocommerce. The two that matter are the exceptions from the Merchant Center client and any invalid Guzzle response, since those carry the actual API error body rather than a status word. Two configuration cases produce this exact silence. First, the site is linked to one Merchant Center account while the domain claim sits on another one, typically after a multi-client account was involved, in which case uploads are accepted and dropped. Second, a reconnect that reauthorised the Google account without restoring the Content API scope: the connection reads as fine, uploads 403 behind the proxy. If the log shows nothing at all for the sync run, that is its own answer, the batch never ran under the account you are looking at, so check whether the completed actions belong to a stale group after the reinstall. title: Forum Guidelines – WordPress.org Forums
text: Forum Guidelines – WordPress.org Forums Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Forum Guidelines Search for: Search forums Forum Guidelines In this article Table of Contents User Expectations Contacting the Moderators Guidelines Do not advertise on the support forums Do not offer to pay for help Do not post about commercial products Do not create multiple accounts Be mindful when creating links to external resources We reserve the right to manage the forums to the best of our ability In closing Last Updated: 25 July 2024 Welcome to the WordPress.org support forums! 😃 The forums is a volunteer-powered resource, available to all users of WordPress to help improve the quality of WordPress Core, plugins and themes and to help solve problems with WordPress. User Expectations As a volunteer-powered forum, users are expected to be kind, helpful and respectful to all, assuming the best intentions of people and trying to help make things better. Please also be aware that these are community forums, this means that all users are required to follow the Community Code of Conduct . Be aware that there is no obligation for support to be provided, including by the developers of themes and plugins hosted on WordPress.org. Be mindful to follow any and all reasonable instructions given by a forum moderator at all times, they are long time contributors with experience to know when action needs to be taken, or warnings need to be issued. Contacting the Moderators If a post needs moderator attention, there is a ‘Report this topic’ link on every thread. That will add the post to a queue moderators watch and follow up with many times a day. If immediate action is needed, or the situation is not limited to a specific post, users should come to Slack and post in the #forums channel. (In many cases, the FAQ already might have an answer to your question. Please remember that the moderators are also volunteer contributors and may not always be online to respond immediately.) Guidelines Do not advertise on the support forums The forums are not a venue to promote your own (or others’) plugins, themes, websites or services. You are also not allowed to request payment to fix someone’s site, please use jobs.wordpress.net for this. Do not offer to pay for help Do not offer to pay for services or help on the forums, please use jobs.wordpress.net for this. Do not post about commercial products Commercial plugins and themes are not sold on WordPress.org, therefore please use their respective websites for support and reviews. For support of commercial themes or plugins, go to their official support channel. In order to be good stewards of the WordPress community, and encourage innovation and progress, we feel it’s important to direct people to those official locations. Doing this will provide the developer with the income they need to make WordPress awesome. Reviews of commercial plugins/themes are acceptable on WordPress.org when such reviews discuss functionality (including Software as a Services [Saas] solutions) or user-facing features. Reviews that are essentially payment disputes or are used to leverage support will be archived, with a reply that such disputes should be handled via private email. Do not create multiple accounts Individuals are limited to a single personal account. A company may register a brand account with a verifiable company email. We do not allow individual users to make multiple accounts, and consider this a bannable offense. Be mindful when creating links to external resources Public links in plugin or theme support topics may only be posted if they meet one or more of the following criteria: The link is to the plugin or theme authors own website. The link is to the plugin or theme authors own support website. The link is posted by the plugin or theme author themselves (or registered support users) to an external resource related to the topic. The link is to resources on the WordPress.org website. The link is to a reputable image-sharing service for screenshots. We reserve the right to manage the forums to the best of our ability We do our best to keep the forums friendly and safe for all users and developers. In order to do so, topic content may be moderated and users may have their access restricted, should the moderation team feel it is appropriate. We aim to use this power lightly and as sparingly as possible, however in severe cases, users may be suspended and posts removed entirely. Common reasons for edits or suspensions include but are not limited to: Violations of the WordPress Community Code of Conduct . Spamming . Unhelpful responses including but not limited to unvetted AI-generated responses or simple copy-and-paste of internet search results that aren’t specifically helpful to the thread starter. Posting personal information of other people (including but not limited to email, name, job, gender, living situation, location, etc). Posting private communication in the public forums or Slack. This includes direct messages, emails, support tickets, or other off-WordPress.org communication. Posting or accepting offers or requests for login information to a site. While plugin and theme authors may ask for this on their own support systems, they may not do so on WordPress.org for liability reasons. Harassment, threats, or abuse via any of WordPress.org’s systems or events (such as meetups or WordCamps). This includes actions such as following people to social media to continue a disagreement or complaint. Posting broad questions about opinions, such as “who is the best web host?” or other similar discussion topics that are not directly related to WordPress, its themes, or plugins. Posting only to solicit feedback for a site, theme, or plugin. Posting in ALL CAPS or abusing formatting (such as bolding the entire topic). Seeking legal advice or threatening legal action, including lawsuits. Please note that neither the list of examples above, or bannable offenses are exhaustive. Each and every post and interaction is judged on its own merits. In closing And that’s all. Enjoy your stay at the forums! Oh.. And, when you’re done, please mark your topic as “Resolved”. Thanks! title: Feed Health Monitor for WooCommerce – WordPress plugin | WordPress.org
text: Feed Health Monitor for WooCommerce – WordPress plugin | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Plugin Directory Feed Health Monitor for WooCommerce Submit a plugin My favorites Log in Submit a plugin My favorites Log in Search plugins Feed Health Monitor for WooCommerce By nersesgh Download Details Reviews Installation Development Support Description Find WooCommerce product data issues that can cause Google Shopping and product feed errors before they hurt your product listings. Find Product Feed Issues Before They Become Problems Feed Health Monitor for WooCommerce scans your WooCommerce catalog for product data issues that can cause products to be rejected, limited, or excluded from product feeds. It helps you identify missing, incomplete, or potentially problematic product information before it affects your product listings on platforms such as Google Shopping. What does it check? The plugin analyzes your WooCommerce products for common feed-related data problems, including: Missing product titles Missing product descriptions Missing product images Missing prices Missing stock information Missing product identifiers Missing or incomplete attributes Product data that may cause feed validation problems Other catalog issues that can affect product feeds Continuous Catalog Monitoring & Workflow (New in 1.3.0) Version 1.3.0 turns Feed Health Monitor into a proactive monitoring tool that runs in the background: * WP-Cron Scheduled Scans: Automatically scan your catalog on a Daily or Weekly cadence using WordPress native cron scheduling without overloading server resources. * Unified Single-Engine Scanning: Scheduled scans run the exact same battle-tested batch validator as manual scans, preventing discrepancy and duplicate logic. * Scan History Archive: Track every completed scan with date, type (Manual vs. Scheduled), product count, healthy items, severity counts, and health score. Includes clean WordPress admin pagination. * Differential Comparison (New vs. Fixed): Compares each completed scan with the immediately previous scan to identify newly introduced problems ( NEW badge) and resolved issues ( FIXED tab) with zero database overhead. * Live Monitoring Dashboard: Real-time monitoring card displaying current status (Active/Disabled), last scan date, next scan date, frequency, current score, score change diff, and counts of new/fixed issues, with quick [Scan Now] and [Monitoring Settings] buttons. * Admin Email Alerts: Notifies store administrators automatically if new critical errors emerge or if catalog health score drops past a configurable threshold. * Data Retention Management: Configurable automatic pruning of historical scan logs (7, 30, or 90 days). Advanced Data Quality Validation Version 1.2.0 introduced deep qualitative checks across your catalog to catch problematic content: * Price Validation: Flags invalid, zero, or negative prices, and alerts when sale prices exceed regular prices. * Title Quality: Identifies suspiciously short or long titles and flags promotional text (e.g. “FREE SHIPPING”, “SALE”). * Description Quality: Flags extremely thin product descriptions. * Image Validation: Checks for valid image URLs and enforces minimum/recommended image dimensions (e.g. 250×250 minimum, 800×800 recommended). * GTIN Validation: Enforces strict GTIN formatting, lengths, and Modulus-10 checksum validation. * Variable Products: Inspects all active variations securely, rolling up grouped errors efficiently without spamming issues. Why use Feed Health Monitor? Instead of discovering product problems after your products have been rejected by a shopping platform, scan your catalog directly from WordPress and identify issues that need attention. Built for WooCommerce Feed Health Monitor works directly with your WooCommerce product catalog and provides a simple way to review product data health from your WordPress dashboard. Google Shopping & Product Feeds Product feed platforms depend on accurate and complete product information. Small catalog issues can result in products being rejected or excluded. Feed Health Monitor helps you find potential problems before they become feed issues. No Feed Generation Required This plugin does not generate product feeds. It focuses specifically on checking the health of your WooCommerce product data so you can identify problems before sending your catalog to external feed platforms. Who is it for? Feed Health Monitor is useful for: WooCommerce store owners Ecommerce managers SEO specialists Google Shopping advertisers Agencies managing WooCommerce stores Developers maintaining product catalogs Free and Lightweight The plugin focuses on catalog health monitoring without adding unnecessary complexity to your WooCommerce store. Install Feed Health Monitor and find product data issues before they become feed problems. Installation Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/feed-health-monitor directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress Navigate to WooCommerce > Feed Health FAQ Does this plugin generate a feed? No, this plugin only monitors your catalog for data issues. How do scheduled scans work? Scheduled scans use standard WordPress Cron (WP-Cron). The background runner uses the existing batch scanner in time-managed chunks to ensure memory and timeout limits are never exceeded, even on huge stores. Reviews There are no reviews for this plugin.
